This class dives into the complete workflow to create and manage security policies for your WAF, helping you address the challenge of blocking malicious traffic without impacting legitimate users. Learn to analyze traffic patterns, write effective rules, and safely test them before going live. From there, we guide you through establishing an iterative process to tune your rules to minimize false positives and eliminate conflicts. sessions.desc: Turn on Cloudflare’s automated protections with confidence, and always know exactly what’s blocking traffic to your zones. This class helps you work with our built-in rulesets and guides you through workflows to audit your configuration, identify false positives, and make narrow rule exceptions instead of disabling protection altogether. Leave with a repeatable cycle to audit, configure, and tune in your own applications. You must bring your laptop to participate in this training.

sessions.title: AppSec: Design rate limiting strategies for complex applications

Also learn how to grant your automated tools their own access without opening a door for users to slip through. Join us to gain design instincts and troubleshooting skills to keep access working as your organization and its systems grow. You must bring your laptop to participate in this training.

Her welcome address highlights the vital, strategic role that partners play in driving Cloudflare's ongoing growth and success.

sessions.title: Reshaping the partner ecosystem for what's next
sessions.desc: The Internet is becoming agentic, and partners are positioned right at the center of it. Enterprises are rearchitecting for an AI-native world, and they need trusted partners to guide them. Cloudflare is the platform they are choosing, and this is the moment for partners to lead. Join Tom Evans, Cloudflare's Chief Partner Officer, as he shares where the ecosystem goes from here. This session provides partners with a clear view of the core pillars of Cloudflare's partner strategy, the AI-first operating model changes that cut friction and grow partner profitability, and the path from partner attach to partner led, on the road to $5 billion and beyond.

sessions.title: Cloudflare OS: Powering the next era of partner-led growth
sessions.desc: Cloudflare OS is the foundational operating system that embeds intelligence, context, and automation to deliver transformative value to the businesses you support. In this session, learn how our unified platform for connectivity, compute, security, and AI serves as the bedrock for partner-driven services and scalable sales motions. Discover how you can leverage Cloudflare OS to build more resilient customer outcomes and a thriving business practice.

sessions.title: Build and sell at the edge: Partnering on Cloudflare’s Developer Platform
sessions.desc: Cloudflare’s Developer Platform is transforming how modern applications are built, deployed, and scaled at the edge. Join Aly Cabral to explore the expanding partner opportunity within Cloudflare’s developer ecosystem, from Cloudflare Workers and AI inference to databases and edge-native architectures. Learn how partners can co-build and co-sell solutions that help customers move faster while unlocking new revenue streams for their own practices. Whether you are building developer-led services or scaling a Cloudflare practice, this session aims to show you how to grow alongside our platform strategy.

sessions.title: Sunbelt Rentals + Adapture: Catching 404s at the edge, one click at a time
sessions.desc: At Sunbelt Rentals, the website's AI chatbot kept producing broken links to product pages. Customers hit dead ends, and revenue leaked away unnoticed. In this session, Muna Khurshid talks with Ankit Dhawan of Sunbelt Rentals and JJ Mocko of Adapture about how they are fixing it with Cloudflare Workers. When a link leads to a missing page, the Worker checks it against Sunbelt's full catalog and redirects visitors to the right page. It also records where they click next, so the redirects get smarter as traffic grows.

sessions.title: Build It — Build durable AI agents with Flue on Cloudflare
sessions.desc: In this hands-on session, build and deploy a durable AI agent using the Flue Framework on Cloudflare Workers. Starting from scratch, create an agent, give it tools to call external APIs, add a sub-agent for delegation, and deploy it live — all powered by Cloudflare Workers Durable Objects for persistence and recovery. We cover the Flue hook model, sandbox strategies, and the deploy-test-iterate loop. Leave with a working agent and patterns to build more. This session is designed for developers and system architects looking to orchestrate reliable AI workflows. You must bring your laptop to participate in this session.

sessions.title: Build It — Deploy your own AI workspace with Cloudflare OS
sessions.desc: Cloudflare OS is an open source AI productivity environment built on Cloudflare Workers. In this hands-on session, deploy your own instance and then customize it with two real changes: configuring a gatekeeper to give your agents safe access to an external service, and writing a custom skill that teaches your agent how your team works. Along the way, learn the architecture — Workers Durable Objects, Dynamic Worker facets, and the gatekeeper security model. Leave with a running, customized instance and the foundation to make it your company’s OS. This session is designed for architects and others working to enable AI productivity at their organizations. You must bring your laptop to participate in this session.

sessions.title: Build It — Workers Previews: Isolated environments for every change your agent makes
sessions.desc: Cloudflare Workers Preview gives every branch a production-like place to run before it ships — its own URL, configuration, bindings, logs, traces, and state — isolated from production and every other change you make. In this hands-on session, you’ll define the starting point every preview branches from and then give one preview its own D1 database or R2 bucket to test configuration and resource changes safely. You’ll leave with a running preview URL and a pre-production feedback loop for agents and humans: deploy, test real behavior, inspect what happened, and verify fixes before they reach production. You must bring your laptop to participate in this session.

sessions.title: 12 mistakes we made building an agent platform for 100,000 employees
sessions.desc: We set out to let any TELUS employee ship a working app as easily as they’d send a link: upload a zip, get a live subdomain, done. But when we tried to make that safe, cheap, and durable for a six-figure user base, we got a dozen things wrong. Join this session for a post-mortem exploration of the decisions we made and what we would do differently. Learn from our mistakes in architecture, security, and trusting an agent — or ourselves — more than we should have. With each mistake, we’ll share the symptoms we saw in production, the fixes that actually worked, and the cheaper signals we ignored beforehand. If you’re building developer infrastructure, an agent runtime, or anything multi-tenant where the tenants are your coworkers, you’ll leave with a checklist of failure modes that you can skip paying for yourself.

sessions.title: After human: How to think about fraud & abuse when anyone could be anything
sessions.desc: Automated traffic has surpassed human traffic on the Internet. The line between human and machine is no longer a reliable signal by itself. This session offers a framework and practical techniques for addressing fraud and abuse when identity, intent, and automation can no longer be taken at face value.

sessions.title: AI, reliability, and the new engineering velocity
sessions.desc: AI is changing how software gets built, reviewed, tested, operated, and improved. But more output does not automatically mean more progress. The engineering leaders who succeed will be the ones who can turn new AI capabilities into durable velocity, while protecting reliability, security, and the long-term health of their codebases and teams. Join leaders from Cloudflare, Block, TELUS Digital, and Hostinger for a candid discussion on the real decisions behind AI-enabled engineering: where to automate, where to keep humans in the loop, how to measure whether AI is creating value, and how to avoid trading short-term speed for long-term complexity. Expect practical lessons, honest anecdotes, and a look ahead at what the engineering organization may become over the next two years.

sessions.title: Building durable agents with Durable Objects
sessions.desc: Durable Objects are the missing primitive for agents: stateful, addressable, isolated services that can live as long as the work requires. In this session, learn how we built an agent cloud entirely on Cloudflare using Durable Objects to model long-lived agents; Cloudflare Workers to compose them; and Cloudflare’s platform for storage, queues, models, artifacts, and sandboxed code execution. Leave this session with a reference architecture for agents that remember, recover, coordinate, and reliably get work done.

sessions.title: Building modern state and local government security without starting over
sessions.desc: The federal government has made zero trust a mandate. The adversaries have made it a necessity. But for state and local governments operating with legacy infrastructure, multi-year procurement cycles, and security teams stretched across dozens of agencies, getting from policy to implementation is the hard part that no framework addresses directly. This panel brings together three of the most operationally experienced public sector security and technology leaders in the country for a practitioner's conversation about what zero trust actually looks like when you have to build it without a federal budget or a CISO team of fifty. Maryland's Secretary of IT, Oklahoma's CISO, and Suffolk County's CTO share direct experience deploying zero trust network access, governing AI tool use across agency workforces, and securing cloud-native infrastructure in environments where the last major system upgrade was a decade ago.

sessions.title: Built differently, secured similarly?
sessions.desc: Just Eat Takeaway.com, Crypto.com, and Moody’s bring perspectives shaped by different industries, threat environments, and regions. Their customers, regulatory obligations, pace of change, and tolerance for disruption differ significantly. Yet their security teams face many of the same decisions on how to keep the business moving through this dynamic landscape. This panel explores where their approaches converge, where they diverge, and what each industry can learn from the other.

sessions.title: Co-engineering the future: How Uber & Cloudflare engineer a global platform
sessions.desc: Uber is reimagining the way the world moves for the better. With over 1 billion monthly active platform consumers and more than 10 million drivers and couriers globally, Uber relies on trusted partners like Cloudflare to deliver solutions today and co-engineer the future. In this fireside chat for platform architects and engineering leaders, Cloudflare VP of Product Steve Goldsmith and Uber VP of Engineering Mattie Toia pull back the curtain on their joint engineering efforts, with detailed technical explanations and anecdotes from real-world delivery experience at Uber and Mattie’s previous experiences with Cloudflare. Leave with concrete insights on balancing security, scale, and high-performance global platform tuning.

sessions.title: Cyber frontier models: How AI is transforming Cloudflare’s security team
sessions.desc: Cloudflare’s security team looks different than it did a year ago. More than 200 agents are now running work that used to be manual, our staff members spend their time differently, and the way we make security decisions has changed. In this session, we share what we’ve actually built, what we’ve learned shipping agents into production, and what’s changed about how the team works. It’s a customer zero look from inside Cloudflare security.

sessions.title: It could happen to you: A Magic Transit Under Attack story
sessions.desc: The prevalence of volumetric attacks continues to increase, and it's easier than ever to launch one. In this session, Cloudflare experts walk through the Magic Transit Under Attack service — a specialized process designed to onboard and protect infrastructure under active DDoS attack. We'll cover the entire workflow from initial hotline contact and traffic analysis to emergency onboarding and mitigation. Leave with a clear understanding of how Under Attack onboarding works and practical insights for network protection.

sessions.title: No Priors: A live conversation with Dane Knecht, CTO of Cloudflare
sessions.desc: What does it look like when the world’s most critical internet infrastructure starts running AI at the edge? No Priors host Sarah Guo sits down Dane Knecht, CTO of Cloudflare, whose network processes over a trillion requests a day, giving him a vantage point on the Internet that almost no one else has. Dane argues that the future of AI isn’t just about massive data centers. It’s about bringing intelligence closer to users and giving developers the tools to build and scale the next generation of applications. He shares why the companies that win the AI era will be the ones that make it easiest for developers to ship, iterate, and grow without getting slowed down by infrastructure. If you’ve ever wondered what the internet looks like from the inside, this episode is a rare look at the layer that could define how AI gets built.

sessions.title: Q-Day is coming: Here’s how to prepare for the threat of a quantum computer
sessions.desc: Join Cloudflare’s Sharon Goldberg as she discusses post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and how to prepare for the threat quantum computers pose to the cryptographic systems that underpin the modern Internet. In this introductory discussion, learn what exactly Q-Day is, how PQC works, and how to prepare your organization for the upgrade to PQC. Hear how Cloudflare has spent the last nine years designing, implementing, and advocating for free, standards-based PQC across the Internet. In early 2026, we revised our Q-Day threat horizon to 2029 and are committed to having all our cryptography fully post-quantum by the end 2029.

sessions.title: Rethinking insider risk for a workforce of people and agents
sessions.desc: Insider risk is one of the hardest problems in security: hard to detect, harder to investigate, and easy to underestimate until it’s too late. This session covers how Cloudflare designed our insider risk program, including the team, the controls we built on top of our own products, and the workflows that connect security with legal, people, and IT. Learn how company-wide AI adoption impacted our insider risk capabilities — which signals weakened, which new categories of risk emerged, and where our detections fell short. Hear how we’ve evolved the program in response and what we think other security teams should be thinking about now.

Join this interactive session to discover how you can automate your entire workflow and start building awesome, production-ready agents today.

sessions.title: System Sketch — Building advanced real-time applications using WebSockets
sessions.desc: Building real-time applications that can handle a variety of situations is challenging. Disconnecting and reconnecting, high latency, and multi-user support all make building performant and reliable applications on Cloudflare a challenge for even the most seasoned developers. In this interactive session, learn how to make the most of the WebSockets API, Cloudflare Developer Platform primitives, and low-latency AI models to build great real-time applications, without incurring big compute bills.

sessions.title: System Sketch — Sandbox egress: Give agents access without giving away the keys
sessions.desc: Agents need to reach external services, but handing credentials directly to untrusted code is a non-starter. Designed for platform engineers and architects building agentic workloads, this interactive session starts with a technical walkthrough of egress controls in Cloudflare Sandboxes and Cloudflare Containers — from deny-by-default networking to programmable outbound handlers that inject secrets at the edge, outside the sandbox boundary. Then, we open the whiteboard to your real architecture questions. How do you scope credentials per session, grant and revoke access at runtime, and prevent data exfiltration without breaking the agent loop? Leave with concrete patterns for safe egress that go well beyond block or allow.

sessions.title: The defender’s clock has collapsed: Securing applications at machine speed
sessions.desc: AI is changing the pace of application security. What once took attackers weeks of research can now happen in minutes or even seconds, shrinking the time organizations have to identify and address risk. In this session, Justin Tibbs, Vice President of Cybersecurity at Presidio, explores how security teams can adapt to a world where both attackers and defenders operate at machine speed. Drawing on Presidio’s work with Project ARGUS, Justin shares how frontier AI can uncover attack paths, business logic flaws, and hidden relationships between vulnerabilities that traditional tools often miss. Get an early look at Presidio’s vision for integrating Project ARGUS with Cloudflare to help bring security insights closer to where applications, APIs, and users connect. This session is sponsored by Presidio.

sessions.title: The economics of model choice: Scaling AI with Nebius and Cloudflare
sessions.desc: Your AI application is gaining users. Do the model choices — and the economics — still make sense? Join Nebius and Cloudflare for a panel about when to consider open models, what drives inference costs beyond the price per token, and how to keep applications secure and reliable as usage grows. We’ll explore where managed inference with Nebius Token Factory fits, what the two companies are learning from working together, and where the partnership could go next. Bring your deployment challenges and help shape the conversation about what’s worth building together. This session is sponsored by Nebius.

sessions.title: Optiv and Cloudflare: Better together
sessions.desc: Implementing, managing, and maintaining security technology is a challenge for even the savviest organizations. Together, Optiv and Cloudflare offer zero trust solutions to help secure networks and applications, no matter where they live. In this session, learn how Optiv security services leverage Cloudflare’s global edge network of 275 data centers in more than 100 countries to improve your defense by extending your security perimeter and blocking attacks at the edge before they ever reach the origin. This session is sponsored by Optiv.

sessions.title: Reach the public without surrendering the data
sessions.desc: NOAA measures the planet obsessively. Getting those measurements in front of the public is the hard part, and it is almost never the rendering. TerraViz is an open source globe that streams Earth science datasets to a browser, a phone, or a headset — no login required. The community demo carries 178 datasets in about 97 GB for a storage bill of $1.31 per month, and egress is unmetered, so cost follows what you publish rather than how many people show up. This demo covers everything wrapped around the globe. Least privilege on a site with no front door, and what broke when authentication covered a whole hostname instead of the two publish paths that needed it. An AI docent built to degrade into determinism rather than answer confidently and incorrectly. Telemetry that stores no IP addresses. And signed node identity, so a museum, a university, and a national lab can share one catalog without sharing a compliance boundary.

sessions.title: Build It — Agent-first development on Cloudflare
sessions.desc: In this hands-on session, set up your coding agent for Cloudflare development using Cloudflare Skills and MCP and then use it to build and deploy a real Worker with a bound KV namespace. We cover how to use Skills effectively, deploy via temporary accounts, and work the agent feedback loop — deploy, verify, read errors, fix, redeploy — until it’s live. Leave with your agent configured, a deployed Worker, and a repeatable workflow for Cloudflare development. You must bring your laptop and to participate in this session.

sessions.title: Build It — Deploy to Void: Launch vibe-coded apps instantly
sessions.desc: Agents make building apps easy. Now, deploy them just as easily. In this session, get an exclusive preview of the new Void deployment platform. Upgrade your vibe-coded apps with Cloudflare’s databases, cron jobs, WebSockets, and more. You must bring your laptop to participate in this session.

sessions.title: Build It — Layered security for your critical web and API assets
sessions.desc: AI-powered exploitation requires hardened protection at the edge before malicious or abusive requests take down your origin. Alongside deploying Cloudflare Web Application Firewall, proactive defense can be added, focusing on protecting your business-critical web and API assets. This follows the best practices of a layered security framework. This interactive session guides you through deploying this proactive layer using Cloudflare’s latest fully automated web asset discovery and profiling. You must bring your laptop to participate in this session.

sessions.title: Catching name collisions before a new gTLD goes live
sessions.desc: ICANN’s next round of the New gTLD Program in 2026 has received over 1,600 applications for new generic top-level domains. Before any go live, ICANN needs to measure name collision risk: queries leaking from private namespaces into the public DNS, where a name that once failed harmlessly suddenly resolves to someone else. This session explains what name collisions are, using real-world examples, and walks through how ICANN evaluates the risk, from the initial collision check to Temporary Delegation and its four operating modes. Leave with a clear picture of the new gTLD timeline, the signals to watch for in your own network, and practical steps to take before a top-level domain you rely on internally becomes a real gTLD.

sessions.title: OneFlare: How Cloudflare and SentinelOne are reshaping complex security
sessions.desc: Environmental complexity is growing, and at the same time attacks are getting faster, more complex, and coming from more directions than ever. Learn how SentinelOne and Cloudflare have partnered to deliver integrations and solutions to help bring enterprise-class automation, network security, and endpoint intelligence and response to any organization. See a deep dive on how SentinelOne’s Automation and Autonomous Security Intelligence work seamlessly with Cloudflare’s Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) and SASE platform to automate detection and response. This session is sponsored by SentinelOne.

sessions.title: The MonkCast from RedMonk
sessions.desc: Join RedMonk, the developer-focused industry analyst firm, to discuss what developer experience means when your users are increasingly AI agents and the “region” you deploy to is the whole planet. Analysts James Governor and Kate Holterhoff sit down for a live recording of The MonkCast, RedMonk’s podcast capturing the candid, off-script “hallway track” of the tech industry with guest Rita Kozlov, VP of Product for Cloudflare’s Developer Platform & AI, who launched Cloudflare Workers and has shaped Cloudflare’s developer strategy ever since — from Pages and D1 to Workers AI. Together they’ll dig into how AI is changing what developers expect from their platforms, why the tools that win will be the ones that remove friction rather than add abstraction, and what it takes to build for both human developers and the agents working alongside them.

sessions.title: 6 architecture patterns that repeat across enterprise customers
sessions.desc: Most enterprise architecture conversations feel unique to the customer, such as for a regulated bank, a multi-tenant SaaS platform, a media business, or a manufacturer. The surface differences (vertical, geography, regulation, and threat model) are real, but the decisions underneath them are mostly the same. After a year of engagements across iGaming, financial services, retail, manufacturing, and media, we have found six patterns surface in nearly every conversation. This session names the six patterns, decomposes the decision underneath each one, and offers questions that surface them earlier in the conversation. This session is ideal for senior architects, infrastructure leads, and IT/security leaders.

sessions.title: A runtime for developers and their agents
sessions.desc: The Cloudflare Workers runtime rests on a few primitives: V8 isolates as the unit of execution, bindings as a capability model instead of ambient network access, conformance to web standards and ECMA-262, and Node.js compatibility. None of these were built with agents in mind. Isolates predate today’s AI by years, and bindings were built to connect a Worker to a database, not sandbox untrusted code. This session covers how these primitives add up to something bigger: a developer platform where human-written and agent-written code run on equal footing. Learn how the web is reshaping around agents as a new kind of visitor and how the developer platform is reshaping around agents as a new kind of developer — one that writes TypeScript to call your tools or completes an entire coding session not typed by hand. Code Mode and the Sandbox SDK are two such examples. The Workers runtime forms the foundation of this evolving developer world view.

sessions.title: Adaptive Intelligence: Detecting sophisticated and persistent attackers
sessions.desc: This session is intended for security professionals and practitioners managing bot threats. There is an open ecosystem devoted to bypassing bot detection — toolkits that forge fingerprints, drive real browsers, and solve challenges automatically. When a detection catches them, contributors patch and ship within days. Against a static defense, every block teaches an attacker exactly where the edges are. Adaptive Intelligence changes the economics: detection signals that keep moving mean attackers can never bank what they learned, making attacks too costly to attempt. Discover why static models have a structural weakness against persistent adversaries and how continuous model retraining and automated disposable rules change attacker economics. Learn what is live today in Cloudflare’s Adaptive Intelligence program and what is coming.

sessions.title: Break the ceiling of internal productivity with a fast, global filesystem
sessions.desc: One of the strongest competitive advantages in this generation of company building is the productivity of your team, in an era where the fastest and leanest teams can outship and outcompete their much larger competitors. This is extremely amplified by AI agents, which can genuinely make teams 10 times more productive. In this session, Jacky Koh, co-founder of Relevance AI, a leading agent-building platform serving agents in production to companies like Databricks, Canva, and Lightspeed, shares the journey of building a new product with the mission of creating a filesystem that maximizes internal productivity. In three months, a team of five working with Cloudflare shipped a full agentic platform across web, desktop, and mobile that has already helped customers replace numerous existing subscriptions and build hyperpersonalized internal tools. Be prepared for a journey and deep dive of technical choices and fun demos.

sessions.title: Cloudflare Workers VPC: Build globally, connect privately
sessions.desc: Cloudflare Workers applications often need to reach APIs and databases that cannot be exposed to the public Internet. Cloudflare Workers VPC connects Workers and Hyperdrive to private networks through existing Cloudflare One connectivity, including Cloudflare Tunnel. This session follows a request from a Worker to a private service: how Cloudflare resolves a private hostname, carries the connection, returns traffic without giving the Worker a stable network identity, and limits access through explicit bindings. It also compares a VPC Service for one approved destination with broader VPC Network access for dynamic destinations, account-wide routes, and Gateway-controlled egress.

sessions.title: Customer zero: How Cloudflare runs AI engineering for 5,000+ employees
sessions.desc: Rolling out coding tools across a company means managing access, context, and cost. This session for engineering and platform leaders shares how Cloudflare built its internal stack using AI Gateway, MCP server portals, and Access, with platform, knowledge, and enforcement layers. Learn from our rollout decisions and setbacks, and see how to adapt the architecture using the Cloudflare Developer Platform and zero trust products. Leave with a reference architecture, a phased rollout plan, and a public checklist for evaluating open source and proprietary coding tools, informed by our focus on open source harnesses.

sessions.title: How publishers can thrive and monetize in the age of AI agents
sessions.desc: Designed for digital publishers, media executives, and web strategists, this session addresses the shift to non-human traffic as it surpasses 50% of all web traffic, threatening traditional ad and referral revenues. Explore how to move beyond basic bot blocking to active enablement, optimization, and value capture. Learn to manage crawler access selectively, track citation rates across AI models via answer engine optimization (AEO), and monetize content through pay-per-use (PPU) micropayments. Leave with strategies to balance content protection with AI discoverability, practical methods to track and boost brand citations in answer engines, and frameworks for unlocking new revenue streams using PPU models.

speakers.name: Lara Cohen
speakers.title: VP of Strategic Partnerships –  Media, Creators & AI

sessions.title: It’s raining AI: Make Cloudflare Developer Platform your umbrella
sessions.desc: In a time when AI is driving relentless experimentation, platform teams face a painful paradox: the business demands both rock-solid uptime and rapid innovation, with less patience for tradeoffs between the two. This session uses Block’s experience to illustrate how platform teams can better balance this squeeze by leveraging Cloudflare Developer Platform.

sessions.title: It’s time to build, not buy
sessions.desc: “Don’t reinvent the wheel” has always been one of the golden tenants of software engineering — but what happens when the wheel becomes really cheap to reinvent? In the past, buying off-the-shelf software almost always made more sense than building something from scratch, but over the last 12 months, the economics have shifted dramatically, and now all it takes is an engineer getting a little too frustrated with janky SaaS software to build a custom replacement in an afternoon. In this talk, we walk through how we’ve been navigating the build-vs.-buy debate at Cloudflare and how it’s changed a lot of our procurement decisions. We use our custom AI code reviewer as a case study of how we built something from the ground up instead of buying something off the shelf, and we discuss the challenges and hurdles we ran into along the way.

sessions.title: Securing your workforce for the AI era
sessions.desc: As organizations scale AI services and internal tools, the access control surface grows faster than policy can keep up. This session walks through a practical workflow for securing your workforce across applications, browsers, and devices. Organize resources and apply policy at the right level of granularity. Enforce step-up authentication where it matters. Make access time-bound so it expires when the job is done. The focus is on composing controls that work together across the stack without creating configuration sprawl or policy debt. Leave this session with a deployable model for tightening security posture across any workload, AI or otherwise.

sessions.title: System Sketch — Everyone can build an app now. Where does it go?
sessions.desc: The number of people who can build prototypes and tools has skyrocketed across every industry. Whether vibe-coded, built with AI, or built the old-fashioned way, these artifacts need a home to be shareable and durable. In this interactive session designed for system architects and operators responsible for hosting applications, we'll explore how platform teams can host these lightweight applications in a way that's secure and scalable without additional overhead. We'll discuss why scaling vertical microservices is the wrong approach for tenant-generated code and how to build a modern, purpose-built control plane. Leave with a concrete architectural blueprint mapping dynamic application hosting to Cloudflare primitives — including Cloudflare Workers for Platforms, Cloudflare Durable Objects, and Cloudflare Workflows.

sessions.title: System Sketch — What just happened? Building replayable event logs for your app
sessions.desc: Every interaction in your app — a user action, an API call, an agent suggestion, or an approval — is an event. Developers typically manage complex infrastructure like Apache Kafka or Apache Spark to distill value from these logs. This session designed for architects and developers explores a pattern for capturing application events as a durable stream stored as compressed Parquet in Cloudflare R2 via Basin Pipelines. We whiteboard the architecture, covering what to log, how to query it with Basin SQL, and how to use it for debugging, compliance, analytics, and letting agents replay past sessions. Leave with a concrete reference architecture and the primitives that make it work.

sessions.title: Transforming enterprise productivity with Cloudflare OS
sessions.desc: Designed for IT leaders and business executives, this session explores how Cloudflare deploys AI internally to drive operational efficiency. Many organizations struggle to integrate AI tools safely without exposing sensitive database perimeters or creating fragmented workflows. Learn how Cloudflare serves as its own most demanding customer through Cloudflare OS, a secure agentic workspace. Discover how we equip employees with automated agent harnesses, secure system-of-record access, and tools like AI-driven sales assistants to streamline the entire customer lifecycle.

sessions.title: We built Signal to not know things. Agents want to know everything.
sessions.desc: The agentic Internet runs on data access — every tool call, trace, and log an agent touches becomes a new surface for leakage and surveillance. Signal took the opposite bet: sealed sender, minimal logs, no contact graphs. Data we never collect can’t leak, be subpoenaed, or stolen. This talk, designed for security leaders and practitioners, maps those lessons onto autonomous systems: where agent metadata concentrates, why tool-call histories are the new metadata goldmine, and three design principles for building useful agents under data minimization. You’ll leave with a checklist for shrinking what your agents can see — and a harder question about what “secure” means when the software acts on its own.

sessions.title: Artifacts: Git-compatible versioned storage, from zero to beta in 3 weeks
sessions.desc: Software engineering has fundamentally changed. In three weeks, our team built and shipped the private beta of Artifacts, Cloudflare’s Git-compatible versioned storage for agents — and AI wrote all the code. But AI alone did not make that possible. Engineers owned the architecture, context, constraints, and verification, while Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects provided proven foundations for scale and trust. In this session, hear the story of building Artifacts from zero to beta, what agentic engineering changed about our roles, and why combining capable agents with Cloudflare’s Developer Platform helps small teams ship ambitious production systems faster than ever.

sessions.title: Beyond IP addresses: Cryptographic primitives for honest bots
sessions.desc: With the rise in traffic from AI agents, it’s no longer clear what’s considered a bot. There are some clearly malicious bots, like ones that DoS your site, and ones that you want, like search engine crawlers. In this session, the Cloudflare research team explains how we are building cryptographic primitives that move automated clients’ legitimacy away from IP addresses and User-Agent rules. Hear about Web Bot Auth and privacy-preserving approaches, why these systems matter as agents multiply across the Internet, and how they can protect origins without weakening users’ privacy. Learn where the proposals stand today, how companies are adopting them, and how website and agent operators can use Cloudflare to prepare.

sessions.title: Building Argus: AI & ML threat detection at scale in Cloudflare
sessions.desc: As Customer Zero, Cloudflare faces unique security challenges at massive scale. Every corporate action flows through Cloudflare Gateway, generating billions of events. To spot critical security threats in this ocean of data, we built Argus. Powered by Spark, Argus uses AI and machine learning to ingest Gateway telemetry alongside other Cloudflare logs like DLP to surface high-fidelity anomalies. Generative AI agents then automatically triage and enrich these alerts, creating a continuous, self-improving defense loop. Discover how we transform our own Zero Trust data into a proactive threat detection engine.

sessions.title: Building secure AI applications on Cloudflare
sessions.desc: In this session we walk through building a secure, scalable application on Cloudflare that leverages AI primitives. Along the way some tips, tricks and facts that can make any application sitting behind Cloudflare more secure!

sessions.title: EmDash: The secure WordPress successor for humans and agents
sessions.desc: WordPress powers 43% of the web but was built for another age. At Cloudflare, we asked, “What would WordPress look like if it were built for the agentic era?” In this talk, Matt Kane (creator of EmDash) introduces EmDash — a full-stack TypeScript CMS powered by Astro and Cloudflare Workers. EmDash keeps what made WordPress successful (extensibility, plugin ecosystem, familiar admin UX) but rebuilds it on secure, sandboxed foundations with agents as first-class citizens.

sessions.title: Merkle Tree Certificates and the next phase of the WebPKI
sessions.desc: Cloudflare has been experimenting with Chrome on the next-generation architecture for post-quantum authentication for the web: Merkle Tree Certificates. Recent developments in quantum technology have led us to expedite the deadline for completing our transition to post-quantum cryptography to 2029. This forces us to shift our focus from harvest-now, decrypt-later attacks to protecting authentication systems from quantum attackers. The cost of post-quantum authentication is the sheer size of digital signatures compared to their classical counterparts, so the primary goal of Merkle Tree Certificates is to reduce the number of signatures needed to establish a connection to a website. In this session, learn about the current deployment status of this new architecture and what clients and site operators need to do to prepare.

sessions.title: Protecting origins in the agentic era
sessions.desc: AI agent traffic is surging, with more than 51% of web traffic being already automated. As agents multiply, origin servers face two to five times load growth. The traditional fix of buying more servers doesn’t scale. This talk walks through how Smart Shield consolidates multiple origin protection capabilities into one platform so that your existing infrastructure can handle the explosion. We’ll show you how Tiered Cache eliminates redundant requests, connection reuse consolidates hundreds of connections into one, Cache Reserve caches long-tail content permanently, and dedicated egress IPs lock down origin access to a limited number of IPs.

sessions.title: Self-hosting Durable Objects
sessions.desc: This session explores the architecture of celld, which allows you to self-host Cloudflare Durable Objects and Cloudflare Workers across many VMs. Learn how this relates to the Deno acquisition and the team’s nascent plans to bring this functionality into workerd.

sessions.title: TanStack Start on Workers: Server-rendering apps an AI just wrote
sessions.desc: In May, Lovable made TanStack Start the default for every new app it generates: rendered on the server, running on Cloudflare Workers. In this session, Lovable Co-Founder and CTO Fabian Hedin explains what that took. He walks through the SSR request lifecycle, including how loaders execute on the server, how dehydrated router state is streamed inline with no client waterfall on first load, and how routes with no data that varies per request are prerendered at deploy time. He also explores how createServerFn is transformed at build time so code meant only for the server never reaches the client bundle, and how secrets scoped to each project live as Worker bindings and rotate without a redeploy. Finally, he discusses the parts that hurt: isolating memory limits, runtime mismatches, and teaching a model a framework that shipped after its cutoff.

sessions.title: Trusting the toolchain: Securing agentic MCP and package registry usage
sessions.desc: An agent is only as trustworthy as the tools, packages, and third-party applications it can call. This session walks through risks associated with agentic tool use: discover and reroute MCP traffic, detect agentic package usage, and limit the scope of impact when a dependency becomes compromised.

sessions.title: Why modern software engineering needs Durable Objects
sessions.desc: As software shifts toward autonomous, long-running agentic systems, traditional stateless serverless architectures are reaching their limits. Modern engineering requires a new default: a persistent, low-latency, colocated state. Join Ashley Peacock, Senior Engineer on the Durable Objects team at Cloudflare, for a practical look at building production-grade, resilient agents on stateful edge infrastructure. Learn how to architect impenetrable systems by taking advantage of recent platform-level enhancements, including built-in platform-driven retries and failure recovery, graceful code deployments that protect long-lived running states, and recent updates to Durable Object lifecycle management. Plus, get an inside look at what’s coming next as we continue to evolve and expand the Durable Objects platform.

sessions.title: Zero trust in railway OT: What worked, what broke
sessions.desc: OT was never built for identity-based access. It ran on implicit trust: physical access was authorization, the wire was the perimeter, IEC 60870-5-104 and Modbus authenticated nothing, and an air gap covered the rest. Add 25-year lifecycles and uptime-over-confidentiality approaches — thinking that IT dropped a decade ago — still running railways. At Estonian Railways, signaling, SCADA, and traffic management need vendor access and patching; and NIS2, IEC 62443, and CLC/TS 50701 expect zones, conduits and auditable access, not a flat VPN. This talk shows what we built on Cloudflare Zero Trust: Cloudflare Tunnel into OT zones, Cloudflare Access policies mapped to IEC 62443 zones/conduits, WARP for engineers, and Cloudflare Gateway logs as audit evidence. Then we cover where zero trust breaks: legacy protocols, latency budgets, safety-certified systems you can’t touch, vendor-mandated jump hosts, and more.

sessions.title: Build It — Deploy your own AI workspace with Cloudflare OS (repeat)
sessions.desc: Cloudflare OS is an open source AI productivity environment built on Cloudflare Workers. In this hands-on session, deploy your own instance and then customize it with two real changes: configuring a gatekeeper to give your agents safe access to an external service, and writing a custom skill that teaches your agent how your team works. Along the way, learn the architecture — Workers Durable Objects, Dynamic Worker facets, and the gatekeeper security model. Leave with a running, customized instance and the foundation to make it your company’s OS. This session is designed for architects and others working to enable AI productivity at their organizations. You must bring your laptop to participate in this session.

sessions.title: Build It — Manage your Cloudflare resources with tags
sessions.desc: Join Senior Product Manager Wesley Evans and Senior Manager of Software Jon Dickson in an interactive demo to learn how to break down your Cloudflare spending across our products using Resource Tagging. This new tagging platform helps you categorize your Cloudflare spending in a way that makes sense for your business. Learn how to create tags and set them on resources like zones, Cloudflare Workers, Cloudflare R2 Storage buckets, and more, and then learn how to understand your spending based on those tagged resources.

sessions.title: Build It — Secure code execution with Cloudflare Sandboxes
sessions.desc: In this hands-on session, you'll build a secure code execution environment using the Cloudflare Sandbox SDK. Starting from a deny-by-default sandbox, you'll configure outbound handlers to inject credentials safely, set host allowlists, and deploy to Cloudflare Workers. We'll cover the security model — isolation, egress control, and access to resources not on the public internet. Designed for developers and platform engineers, you'll leave with a deployed, secure sandbox and patterns to run untrusted code safely. Bring your laptop; a laptop is required to participate.

speakers.name: Damon LaCaille
speakers.title: Principal Solutions Architect – AI and Dev Platform

speakers.name: Felipe Ryan
speakers.title: Principal Solution Architect, AI and Dev Platform

sessions.title: From AI mandate to AI value:The Forward Deployed playbook for enterprise AI
sessions.desc: Every enterprise has an AI mandate. Few have a path to value. The gap between AI ambition and business impact isn’t a technology problem — it’s an execution problem. In this session, Accenture shares how its Forward Deployed model is closing that gap: embedding practitioners directly inside client environments to translate strategy into working systems, measurable outcomes, and self-sustaining capability. Drawing on cross-industry deployments across software, data, and cloud platforms, we’ll unpack the playbook — from aligning AI initiatives to enterprise priorities, to navigating the organizational friction that stalls even the best-funded programs. You’ll leave with a practical framework for moving AI from boardroom mandate to bottom-line value — faster, with less waste, and built to scale. This session is sponsored by Accenture.

speakers.name: Ram Ramalingam
speakers.title: Global Lead – Software & Platforms Engineering & FDE

sessions.title: When an agent behaves differently: Detecting risk beyond the prompt
sessions.desc: Prompt inspection alone does not reveal whether an agent has become risky. This session introduces behavior-based signals for agentic systems: anomalous token use, unexpected delegation chains, repeated failed requests, off-hours activity, and changes in tool-use patterns. Learn how these signals complement identity and policy controls, giving security teams a way to investigate agents that are authorized but behaving outside their expected roles.

sessions.title: Application Security Associate certification exam
sessions.desc: The Cloudflare Application Security Associate certification gives customers, partners, and practitioners formal proof of their Cloudflare AppSec expertise, strengthening hiring decisions, accelerating product adoption, and reducing misconfiguration risk in production. This proctored exam session — designed for security professionals, developers, and administrators with hands-on Cloudflare experience — covers WAF, DDoS, bot management, API security, and analytics. Leave with an industry-recognized Cloudflare credential, a Credly badge, and the validation of practical AppSec skills.

sessions.title: Zero Trust Associate certification exam
sessions.desc: The Cloudflare Zero Trust Associate certification validates the skills practitioners need to move organizations off legacy VPNs and onto modern ZTNA, addressing one of the most urgent transitions in enterprise security today. This proctored exam session — designed for security analysts, network engineers, and partner SEs with one to two years of hands-on experience — covers zero trust concepts, identity, the Cloudflare One Client, Cloudflare Tunnel connectors, traffic policies, and Cloudflare Access. Gain a recognized Cloudflare credential and a Credly badge as well as confidence implementing zero trust on the Cloudflare One platform for clients or your own organization.

sessions.title: System Sketch — Take control of your AI: Governance for models and tools
sessions.desc: AI adoption is moving fast, but unmonitored model usage and rogue tool execution bring serious security, cost, and compliance risks. Join us for an interactive, hands-on whiteboard session where we break down how to build a robust governance layer for your organization using Cloudflare AI Gateway and Cloudflare MCP server portals.

speakers.name: Chelsee Purvis
speakers.title: Senior Cloudflare One Specialist Solutions Engineer

sessions.title: 100 billion profiles, one early bet on Cloudflare Durable Objects
sessions.desc: In this fireside chat, Mark Dembo, Head of Solutions for Cloudflare's developer platform, sparks a conversation with Alexander Braunreuther, Chief Architect at Contentful, about being a first mover and why it was worth it. Alex talks through the early Cloudflare Durable Objects bet: the speed and scale it unlocked, the missing features his team built themselves, and the collaboration with Cloudflare that closed the gaps.

sessions.title: 5 questions every CTO must answer about AI agents
sessions.desc: Your business units are already building AI agents, each on a different platform, with their own identity, logging, and bill. That speed creates blind spots, runaway cost, and compliance gaps with no clear ownership. This session for CTOs and technology leaders reframes the problem as five questions every leader should be asking: How do agents connect? Who do they act as? What stops them from doing harm? What can they see? How much do they cost? The answer is a consistent way to govern agents regardless of the platform they run on, instead of maintaining one policy per team. Learn about where the controls are real today and explore a vendor-agnostic solution blueprint to connect, secure, and govern your multi-platform agentic AI strategy

sessions.title: Cloudflare OS: Automating work with agents connected to your systems
sessions.desc: Employees want AI that can reach internal systems, and handing out API keys doesn’t scale. Cloudflare OS is an open source agent workspace your company owns and runs. Your teams work with agents that know your organization’s context and reach internal systems through brokered access, producing documents, applications, and workflows that automate recurring work. In this session, watch Cloudflare experts build an app live on stage against a real system of record, learn how per-resource access and model routing keep data and costs under control, and hear about what worked and what didn’t rolling this out at Cloudflare. This session is geared toward IT, security, and platform teams responsible for how their company adopts AI.

sessions.title: Deploying a WAF vs. running a WAF program: The missing manual
sessions.desc: You have a WAF. But can you say whether it’s covering every public-facing asset, actively blocking versus just watching, or quietly bypassed since the last review? Most security teams can’t. In this session, IONIX CTO, Billy Hoffman, and Presidio's VP of Cybersecurity, Justin Tibbs, share IONIX’s WAF Program Maturity Model — a framework that scores WAF programs across ten dimensions, from asset visibility to program ownership, against three maturity stages. Each stage lays out exactly what to fix next: know what should be protected, prove it is, and then make policy compliance the default and mitigation a matter of hours. IONIX and Presidio unpack the challenges that shape early programs and the practical steps that move teams to continuous, provable coverage. Walk away with a self-assessment framework and a next-step roadmap for any WAF you’ve deployed. This session is sponsored by IONIX.

sessions.title: How the Internet really works: Into the depths of Internet infrastructure
sessions.desc: You might have heard statements like "70% of Internet traffic passes through Northern Virginia" or that satellite communications are how intercontinental communication happens. Would it surprise you that neither of those statements is true? This talk dives into the depths of how Internet infrastructure is all around you, what actually carries your Internet traffic, and how a network like Cloudflare is perfectly suited for the evolving demands of Internet infrastructure with AI.

sessions.title: Move fast, stay reliable: Cloudflare’s multilayer resilience strategy
sessions.desc: This session pulls back the curtain on Cloudflare’s resilience-focused engineering strategy, detailing Cloudflare’s high availability, disaster recovery, business continuity, and safe change efforts. Discover how Cloudflare proactively validates its systems through real-world chaos engineering — including automated top-of-rack testing and weekly cut tests — and how our team is reducing engineer-driven incidents and the scope of impact. Leave with an inside look at how Cloudflare’s rollout safety, service-level segmentation, and other resilience efforts are coming together with chaos engineering to prevent, detect, and isolate issues and eliminate the global scope of impact.

speakers.name: Nayla Raad
speakers.title: Director, Product Management – Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery

sessions.title: People, devices, and agents: How Rippling’s edge architecture evolved
sessions.desc: Rippling’s use of Cloudflare Workers began as a simple multi-region routing layer for people. It evolved into a stateful platform for device management, using Durable Objects and hibernated WebSockets to push commands reliably. Today, Workers powers Rippling’s AI infrastructure, including MCP gateway, third-party MCP governance, and AI policy and budget controls. This talk traces Rippling’s journey from routing people to managing devices and governing agents at the edge.

sessions.title: Prevent, don’t detect: Introducing Cloud Workload Security
sessions.desc: Today, cloud security mostly works by detection. Something gets misconfigured, a tool flags it, and someone chases it down. By then, the risky configuration is already live and on the path to exploitation. Cloud Workload Security (CWS) is a new addition to the Cloudflare One platform. It’s a modern inline proxy for the cloud that stops insecure configurations and unapproved actions before they are executed by the cloud provider, across build, deploy, and runtime. In this session, we launch CWS, walk through the use cases driving early adoption, and show where it fits alongside your existing cloud security stack.

sessions.title: Rebuilding legacy software for the AI era
sessions.desc: AI has already changed how individual developers write software. The bigger question is what it changes at the level of systems, teams, and strategy. This session is for developers and engineering leaders responsible for mature software. Using vinext, a cleanroom reimplementation of Next.js built in months, we explore how AI makes previously impractical rewrites possible, why test suites and conformance become strategic assets, and how teams can move quickly without losing control. Leave with a framework for finding the right opportunities and deciding when to maintain, modernize, or replace the software they depend on.

sessions.title: Securing Internet traffic for the quantum computing era
sessions.desc: Post-quantum encryption is moving from research topic to operational reality, but deploying new cryptography across the Internet requires more than flipping a switch. This session is for security, networking, and infrastructure teams planning for post-quantum migration. Walk through Cloudflare’s lessons from rolling out post-quantum protection at scale, including how we built our system to test compatibility, understand performance tradeoffs, support adoption, monitor failures, and communicate risk. Leave this session with practical guidance for making post-quantum encryption real in production environments and an understanding of how Cloudflare accomplished this work based on our automatic SSL/TLS system and how it is protecting customers (and speeding them up) at scale.

sessions.title: SocialKit: AI social toolset built on Cloudflare
sessions.desc: Agents are easy to demo and hard to run. SocialKit runs for real: a full AI agent that writes, designs, and schedules social posts, generating words, images, and full videos entirely on Cloudflare, with no servers and no GPUs. This session shows developers and architects the architecture that makes it work: durable agent state in Cloudflare D1, coordination in Durable Objects, media rendered with Workers, Containers, and Queues, and every model call through AI Gateway, all scaling from zero to bursts automatically. We’ll follow one post from prompt to published and show what held up under load. You’ll leave the session with a reference architecture, the agentic patterns, and a playbook to ship your own.

speakers.name: Matan Lachmish
speakers.title: Founder of Taka.ai, Entrepreneur in Residence

sessions.title: Your AI agent is a distributed system
sessions.desc: AI agents look simple in a demo: give a model some tools and let it run. Production changes the problem completely. Agents need durable state, retries, scheduling, concurrency, real-time communication, observability, and a way to survive failures without losing their place. In other words, they start looking a lot like distributed systems. This session explores the infrastructure patterns behind reliable, long-running agents, what we’ve learned building them at Cloudflare, and how those lessons change the way developers should think about agent architecture.

sessions.title: Securing open source websites at scale with edge-first defense
sessions.desc: Open source powers much of the web, and its transparency is a security strength: code is publicly reviewed, flaws are disclosed openly, and patches ship fast. But openness alone does not stop bots, DDoS attacks, or zero-day exploits at scale. This session is for security leaders and web architects running many sites on open source content platforms. Shane Jordan, Senior Product Manager at Acquia, shares how pairing a community-audited platform with edge-based defense creates layered protection that supports compliance goals. Learn how open security practices reduce risk, which protections belong at the edge versus the application, and how to apply consistent policy across many sites at once. This session is sponsored by Acquia.

sessions.title: Trust in the agent era: Why a year of ordinary behavior beats verification
sessions.desc: Attackers can spoof a device, rotate an IP, script a browser, and defeat a liveness check. While agents have made impersonation fast and near free, what no attacker can cheaply manufacture is a year of ordinary behavior. This session covers how Cloudflare establishes trust per account and reevaluates it as behavior changes. Learn how this approach exposes account takeover, fake signups, and coordinated fraud rings without adding friction for real customers.

sessions.title: Latent.Space: Live interview with Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht
sessions.desc: Join the hosts of Latent.Space for a live podcast recording at Cloudflare Connect featuring Cloudflare Chief Technology Officer (CTO) Dane Knecht. Geared toward AI engineers and technical builders, this episode explores how rapidly evolving industry trends are reshaping application architecture, transitioning from simple model completions to autonomous, tool-using agentic workflows. As AI development shifts beyond centralized LLM APIs toward complex, multi-agent orchestration, developers face critical bottlenecks around latency, state management, and real-time execution. In this conversation, Dane Knecht breaks down how the industry is adapting its stack to run AI workloads at the network edge, bringing model execution and dynamic tool calling milliseconds away from end users.

sessions.title: Closing the loop: Agentic threat intelligence and threat response
sessions.desc: Security teams are drowning in two asymmetries: attackers move at machine speed, while analysts triage and write intelligence at human speed. This session presents two production systems — built entirely on Cloudflare’s developer platform — that close that gap by embedding agentic-driven agents on both sides of the defensive lifecycle: threat intelligence agents that reason over what we know, and threat response agents that act on what we find. On the response side: a lightweight endpoint agent that streams forensic artifacts where an agentic pipeline extracts IOCs and enriches them. On the intelligence side: software that turns enrichment output into finished reporting.

speakers.name: Javier Castro
speakers.title: Senior Director of Engineering — Cloudforce One

sessions.title: Cloudflare OS is an architecture of distrust
sessions.desc: "Cloudflare OS is an architecture of distrust." At least, that’s what an AI said when it reviewed the code, because Cloudflare OS is designed to distrust the AI. Most agent harnesses these days simply give the AI free rein and pray for alignment. Cloudflare OS is different. It implements an extensive set of guardrails that make it nearly impossible for the AI to make serious mistakes. The goal: you should be able to give Cloudflare OS to anyone at your company while allowing your security and compliance teams to sleep at night. Kenton Varda is the architect of these guardrails (and the architect of the Cloudflare Workers platform). In this talk, he will walk through all of the details. Learn why an AI described the capability-based security model as a “leash” and the sandbox a “cage,” and discover how the system sets up a “fabricated reality” for the agent that relieves the human operator from having to supervise every action.

sessions.title: Connecting Cloudflare One data protection and secure AI
sessions.desc: As AI becomes embedded in everyday work, security teams need a way to protect sensitive data without slowing adoption. This session explores how Cloudflare One data protection capabilities and secure AI controls can work together to provide visibility, policy enforcement, and practical guardrails across users, applications, and AI services. Learn how to reduce exposure, govern sensitive interactions, and create a more consistent control model for AI-driven workflows. The focus of this session is on real-world implementation patterns that help practitioners connect data protection and secure AI into a single, operational approach that supports both security and productivity.

sessions.title: From 76% to 100% cache hits: Rebuilding docs caching on Cloudflare
sessions.desc: Mintlify serves over 200 million monthly page views across thousands of developer docs sites, and our Next.js ISR caching couldn’t keep up with deploy velocity. Nearly one in four visitors hit a cold start, and our cache hit rate was stuck at 76%. This session shares the engineering story of how we rebuilt our caching layer on Cloudflare: a Worker proxy in front of all traffic, version-aware cache keys for HTML and RSC, webhook-driven revalidation, Durable Objects for distributed locking, and Cloudflare Queues for batched cache warming. With these, we effectively reached a 100% cache hit rate. You’ll leave this session with concrete, reusable patterns for caching a high-velocity multi-tenant app at the edge.

sessions.title: From intent to infrastructure: Rethinking CDN resiliency with AI
sessions.desc: CDN configurations encode the same delivery intent in vendor-specific ways, making migrations and multi-CDN operations slow and risky. In this session, Cloudflare introduces an intent-driven approach: define behavior once, use AI to generate reviewable tests and candidate configuration, and validate the result with end-to-end evidence in an isolated environment. Through a live demo, see how human approval, deterministic safeguards, and automated recovery turn configuration into a test-driven workflow. Built for infrastructure architects and SREs, this session offers a practical model for owning intent and tests while vendors implement against a shared behavioral contract.

sessions.title: How Figma runs AI-generated code on Cloudflare
sessions.desc: AI-generated code needs a place to run. This session follows a request through Nimbus, Figma’s sandbox platform, showing how Cloudflare Workers, Cloudflare Durable Objects, and Cloudflare Containers connect an AI coding workflow to a live browser preview. Developers will see a working demo and learn three practical patterns: allocating isolated compute, routing interactive preview traffic, and using warm sandboxes to reduce startup waits.

sessions.title: Inside United Airlines: How a global airline is rethinking cyber defense
sessions.desc: Few companies run operations as complexly or as closely watched as United Airlines. Sean Mason, Head of Cyber Defense for United, joins Rohit Chenna Reddy, Security Strategy Lead at Cloudflare, for a candid fireside chat on how his team is rethinking cyber defense at one of the world’s largest airlines. Sean unpacks the complexity of securing an airline, shares how his team is changing its approach, and explores how AI and other emerging technologies are reshaping how defenders find and respond to threats.

speakers.name: Rohit Chenna Reddy
speakers.title: Security Strategy & CSO Chief of Staff

sessions.title: MCP made it easy, and that’s the problem
sessions.desc: Standing up an MCP server used to be a project, which meant someone had to decide what agents should actually be allowed to do. Cloudflare’s one-click WebMCP support makes it a toggle, and that decision is now unguarded. This session is a field report from the other side of that toggle: our own MCP server, over our own content, exposed through the WebMCP preview. What belongs behind /mcp depends on what an agent takes from you, and retailers, publishers, and services organizations get three very different answers. Learn how to address tool responses that strip away every cue a person uses to judge a page, and develop a strategy for content nobody has audited that comes back fast, clean, and confidently wrong.

sessions.title: Monetizing AI agent traffic: Write your first Monetization Gateway rule
sessions.desc: The majority of Internet traffic is now driven by AI agents, which means that businesses must learn how to charge AI agents for their consumption. In this session, developers and business strategists will learn how to set up their first monetization rule in the Cloudflare Monetization Gateway, experiment with pricing strategies, and track what agents actually pay for.

sessions.title: Rearchitecting the Cloudflare network for the AI revolution
sessions.desc: Join this session to walk through the Cloudflare operations infrastructure. The session starts with a historical look back and ends with outlining the ongoing work in modernizing the Cloudflare Global Network.

sessions.title: Unifying network observability: Logs, traces, and the agents you run
sessions.desc: This session is tailored for developers, platform teams, and security engineers who troubleshoot on Cloudflare. Logs, analytics, traces, and alerts have lived in separate products with separate query languages, so one question means multiple tabs. This session shows what changes when they become one product and what benefits it brings: one query language to learn, answers without standing up a pipeline first, and alerts on anything you can query. Also learn about observability for the AI agents you build on Cloudflare Workers and where the network starts fixing what it can on its own. You will leave knowing what this replaces in your setup and how to get your telemetry into the tools you already run.

speakers.name: Rian van der Merwe
speakers.title: Senior Director of Product, Data & Observability

sessions.title: Why our scale, reach, and breadth aren’t easily replicable
sessions.desc: For infrastructure, operations, architecture, and IT/security leaders, network choice increasingly shapes application performance, resilience, reputation, and the ability to scale. This session examines how Cloudflare built a globally connected network through a disciplined and principled network strategy and not simply capital spending. Learn why durable network scale compounds over time, how free plans and customer traffic strengthen the platform, and what this means for organizations building for an AI-driven future. Leave with a framework for evaluating infrastructure advantages and making platform decisions that support sustainable growth.

speakers.name: Shozo Moritz Takaya
speakers.title: Infrastructure Strategy Manager, EMEA · Global Network Strategy

sessions.title: The four jobs of a machine payment
sessions.desc: When an AI agent pays for something, it has to do four things: prove who it is, stay within its budget, pay across any network, and settle, sometimes for a fraction of a cent. Join this panel session to hear leaders from Mastercard, Ant International, and Coinbase will talk through how Mastercard’s Agent Pay for Machines (AP4M) handles each step, and what still has to happen before agents can pay as easily as people do.

sessions.title: When AI finds vulnerabilities faster than you can patch
sessions.desc: Frontier AI is changing the economics of vulnerability research. As vulnerabilities are discovered and weaponized faster, patching cadence must become an architectural consideration. This session presents a defense-in-depth pattern for protecting Internet-facing workloads on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) during the interval between vulnerability identification and completed remediation. Explore how secure OCI landing zones, workload isolation, identity controls, asset inventory, automated patch rings, and continuous validation establish the foundation. Then, see how Cloudflare protections can reduce externally reachable attack paths while patches are tested and deployed. Using a realistic vulnerability-response scenario, learn how to select compensating controls, measure residual risk, prevent origin bypass, accelerate remediation, and retire temporary protections once the underlying vulnerability has been fixed. This session is sponsored by Oracle.

sessions.title: Build It — Build durable AI agents with Flue on Cloudflare (repeat)
sessions.desc: In this hands-on session, build and deploy a durable AI agent using the Flue Framework on Cloudflare Workers. Starting from scratch, create an agent, give it tools to call external APIs, add a sub-agent for delegation, and deploy it live — all powered by Cloudflare Workers Durable Objects for persistence and recovery. We cover the Flue hook model, sandbox strategies, and the deploy-test-iterate loop. Leave with a working agent and patterns to build more. This session is designed for developers and system architects looking to orchestrate reliable AI workflows. You must bring your laptop to participate in this session.

sessions.title: Build It — Deploy AI safely with Cloudflare
sessions.desc: Get hands-on with Cloudflare to safely adopt AI across your workforce and applications. In this session, learn how to discover shadow AI usage, steer employees toward approved AI tools, and prevent sensitive data from being shared with public AI services. Then, explore how the same zero trust controls extend to privately deployed AI tools and agents using Cloudflare AI Gateway and DLP profiles to help secure AI traffic, giving teams the visibility, policy enforcement, and data protection they need to move quickly with AI. You must bring your laptop to participate in this session.

sessions.title: Build It — Protect your internal or external AI- or LLM-powered apps now
sessions.desc: As application functionalities increasingly become AI- or LLM-powered to enhance the end user experience, signature-based security falls short. To maintain the same security standard, novel approaches are required. This interactive session showcases various real-life AI/LLM application examples and how to define security rules to guard each of them. The ultimate goal is top-notch security that does not need to slow down innovations. You must bring your laptop to participate in this session.

sessions.title: System Sketch — Agents that talk: Building a voice agent on Cloudflare
sessions.desc: As agent capabilities grow, developers are reaching for dynamic, real-time interfaces that can keep up. Voice control has emerged as one of the strongest and most capable ways to quite literally chat with your AI applications. In this session, we use Cloudflare’s advanced voice SDKs and network to build low-latency, voice-powered AI agents. Learn how to use Flue and the Cloudflare Developer Platform to ship your own AI agent that can hear and speak, integrating common tools to give it access to the web at large.

sessions.title: System Sketch — Connecting the pieces: Using Bindings to build an application on Cloudflare
sessions.desc: The bindings model is core to the Cloudflare Developer Platform: with just a few lines of code, you can connect databases, AI inference, and even other applications. Bindings aren't just good developer experience, they also have interesting security and performance characteristics that make them a unique part of building on Cloudflare. In this interactive session, we'll cover how to build a fully featured application on Cloudflare, making use of bindings to connect different parts of the platform. Bring your laptop — let's get coding!

sessions.title: System Sketch — Securing AI in practice
sessions.desc: AI has rapidly moved from experimentation into the workflows your employees use every day, including customer-facing products. Organizations of all types and sizes need to secure systems that access sensitive data, use tools, and take action. In this interactive discussion, we'll discuss how the security landscape is evolving, where familiar controls already apply, and how to implement visibility, control, and isolation in your own environment. Explore real-world scenarios and examine practical patterns for reducing risk without slowing AI adoption. This interactive session is designed for security professionals, system architects, and developers tasked with governing AI platform integrations.

sessions.title: Advancing open AI infrastructure through community & ecosystem collaboration
sessions.desc: Join MiTAC Computing to explore full-stack open AI infrastructure — integrating compute, storage, networking, liquid cooling, and orchestration. Discover how open source firmware (e.g., OpenBMC, OPF) and open AI platforms accelerate energy-efficient, interoperable, and scalable enterprise AI deployments. This session is sponsored by MiTAC Computing.

sessions.title: Building P1 on Cloudflare: AI-native web composition and governance
sessions.desc: In 2025, Pantheon partnered with Cloudflare to power its global edge. Using Cloudflare primitives on the Cloudflare Development Platform, Pantheon scaled a great idea into an entirely new enterprise-grade product, P1, that is transforming how organizations build and run websites — in only seven months. In this session, Chris Yates, Pantheon’s SVP of Product, Design, and Engineering, shares the architecture behind P1. Learn how Pantheon combined Cloudflare Workers, Cloudflare Durable Objects, Cloudflare Workflows, Cloudflare Workers AI, Cloudflare AI Gateway, Cloudflare R2, and Cloudflare D1 to create an AI harness for human and agent workflows. Discover how to compose edge primitives, route models, and scale velocity without multiplying risk.

speakers.name: Chris Yates
speakers.title: SVP of Product, Design, and Engineering

sessions.title: Cloudflare Workers monorepo
sessions.desc: Most teams run a handful of Cloudflare Workers and deploy them with wrangler deploy. At Block, we manage 216+ Cloudflare Workers across multiple accounts and business units all from a single monorepo. This talk walks through the architecture, tooling, and organizational patterns that let a small platform team provide a consistent, self-service management experience for every Worker in the fleet, regardless of which team owns it.

sessions.title: Developer tooling in the agentic era
sessions.desc: AI is changing how software is created, but generating more code does not automatically help teams ship better products. Developers still need fast feedback loops, reliable infrastructure, and tools they can understand and trust. Drawing on his experience creating Vue.js and Vite and building VoidZero, Evan You will explore how developer tooling, in particular for web developers, must evolve for an AI-native future. Learn about the move toward unified, high-performance toolchains, the continued importance of open source, and what it takes to build tools used by developers around the world.

sessions.title: Giving an agent 10,000 tools with Code Mode
sessions.desc: How do you give an AI agent access to 10,000 tools without filling its context window? Let it write code. This session explores using Code Mode through Executor to discover tools on demand, combine API calls, and process results in a sandbox. Through a live demo built on Cloudflare, learn the architecture, tradeoffs, and approval controls behind this approach. You’ll leave with practical patterns for connecting agents to large tool catalogs while keeping execution efficient and permissions explicit.

sessions.title: How we built Cloudflare’s global network
sessions.desc: Learn how Cloudflare built and continues to expand one of the world’s largest global networks — spanning more than 330 cities across more than 120 countries. Discover how we think about data center placement, peering and interconnection strategy, and traffic engineering, and learn about the policy considerations that shape building a network at global scale.

sessions.title: MCP is the door, and the control plane is the house
sessions.desc: MCP makes it easy to connect agents to tools. That is both the unlock and the danger. At Cloudflare, we connected internal agents to systems like GitLab, Backstage, Jira, Sentry, Prometheus, Google Workspace, and our internal Release Manager. It quickly became clear that the hard problem was not “can the agent call a tool?” It was “which tool, for which user, under which policy, with what context cost, and what scope of impact?” This talk covers MCP at enterprise scale: how we use Cloudflare Access for identity, MCP server portals for governance, Code Mode to reduce token overhead, and sandboxed execution to constrain what model-generated code can do.
