We share lessons from running MCP internally and why unmanaged MCP becomes entropy surprisingly fast.

sessions.title: Ready for shopping season: Verifying and authorizing buying agents
sessions.desc: 2026 is the year of the agent. At Experian, we think it ends as the year of the shopping agent. Bot managers block non-browser traffic by default, so agents carrying real revenue get blocked with the bad bots. Admitting the good ones requires answering four questions. Cloudflare’s Web Bot Auth answers one: did this key send this request unmodified? Experian Agent Trust answers the other three: is a verified human bound to the agent, is there approval of the exact cart, and is there no sign of hijacking? In this session, we build all four at the Cloudflare edge on Workers and Durable Objects and then stress-test them live: unknown agent, replay, repriced cart, and weak human binding. Nothing is charged. Leave with the reference architecture and a clear understanding of what each layer catches.

sessions.title: Shrinking the scope of impact: Controls for AI-era cyber resilience
sessions.desc: This session is intended for security architects and platform engineers. AI is compressing the window between vulnerability disclosure and exploitation, outpacing patch cycles. Using JPMorganChase’s cyber resilience guidance as a framework, this session walks through a blueprint on Cloudflare to implement and automate five high-leverage controls that contain the scope of impact across AI agent sandboxing with policy-bound egress, network security workload egress filtering, web application security, and identity-based zero trust access controls. See how unifying these controls with reusable policies helps mitigate risks faster than traditional approaches.

sessions.title: TanStack Start, and the rest of the TanStack ecosystem
sessions.desc: TanStack Start is a full-stack framework for React and friends, sitting on top of the rest of TanStack: Query, Router, Table, Form, DB, and more. This session is a tour of Start and the ecosystem around it: how the pieces fit, what it feels like to build with them, and where the stack is headed.

sessions.title: The rogue agent problem: When AI adoption outpaces your security
sessions.desc: AI adoption doesn't roll out — it spreads. One approved tool becomes ten unapproved ones. One experiment becomes a production deployment nobody secured. For security investigation and response teams, every ungoverned AI deployment is a blind spot — new attack surface you can't monitor, new data flows you can't inspect, and new behaviors your detections weren't built to catch. This session covers the real patterns behind AI sprawl — shadow AI, ungoverned deployments, supply chain risk, and data leakage — through the lens of security investigations and incident response. We'll share the frameworks Cloudflare's security response team built to identify, investigate, and respond to AI-driven risk at scale.

sessions.title: Application Security Associate certification exam
sessions.desc: The Cloudflare Application Security Associate certification gives customers, partners, and practitioners formal proof of their Cloudflare AppSec expertise, strengthening hiring decisions, accelerating product adoption, and reducing misconfiguration risk in production. This proctored exam session — designed for security professionals, developers, and administrators with hands-on Cloudflare experience — covers WAF, DDoS, bot management, API security, and analytics. Leave with an industry-recognized Cloudflare credential, a Credly badge, and the validation of practical AppSec skills.

sessions.title: Zero Trust Associate certification exam
sessions.desc: The Cloudflare Zero Trust Associate certification validates the skills practitioners need to move organizations off legacy VPNs and onto modern ZTNA, addressing one of the most urgent transitions in enterprise security today. This proctored exam session — designed for security analysts, network engineers, and partner SEs with one to two years of hands-on experience — covers zero trust concepts, identity, the Cloudflare One Client, Cloudflare Tunnel connectors, traffic policies, and Cloudflare Access. Gain a recognized Cloudflare credential and a Credly badge as well as confidence implementing zero trust on the Cloudflare One platform for clients or your own organization.

sessions.title: Build It — Deploy your own AI workspace with Cloudflare OS (repeat)
sessions.desc: Cloudflare OS is an open source AI productivity environment built on Cloudflare Workers. In this hands-on session, deploy your own instance and then customize it with two real changes: configuring a gatekeeper to give your agents safe access to an external service, and writing a custom skill that teaches your agent how your team works. Along the way, learn the architecture — Workers Durable Objects, Dynamic Worker facets, and the gatekeeper security model. Leave with a running, customized instance and the foundation to make it your company’s OS. This session is designed for architects and others working to enable AI productivity at their organizations. You must bring your laptop to participate in this session.

sessions.title: Build It — Layered security for your critical web and API assets (repeat)
sessions.desc: AI-powered exploitation requires hardened protection at the edge before malicious or abusive requests take down your origin. Alongside deploying Cloudflare Web Application Firewall, proactive defense can be added, focusing on protecting your business-critical web and API assets. This follows the best practices of a layered security framework. This interactive session guides you through deploying this proactive layer using Cloudflare’s latest fully automated web asset discovery and profiling. You must bring your laptop to participate in this session.

sessions.title: Build It — Secure code execution with Cloudflare Sandboxes (repeat)
sessions.desc: In this hands-on session, you'll build a secure code execution environment using the Cloudflare Sandbox SDK. Starting from a deny-by-default sandbox, you'll configure outbound handlers to inject credentials safely, set host allowlists, and deploy to Cloudflare Workers. We'll cover the security model — isolation, egress control, and access to resources not on the public internet. Designed for developers and platform engineers, you'll leave with a deployed, secure sandbox and patterns to run untrusted code safely. Bring your laptop; a laptop is required to participate.

speakers.name: Damon LaCaille
speakers.title: Principal Solutions Architect – AI and Dev Platform

speakers.name: Felipe Ryan
speakers.title: Principal Solution Architect, AI and Dev Platform

sessions.title: Beyond “Are you human?” Advanced strategies for managing agentic traffic
sessions.desc: AI-driven bots have evolved from simple scrapers to sophisticated agents that scrape data at mass speed and scale to train AI models. This session explores how web application owners can gain visibility and control over agentic traffic through a modern lens of risk and trust. We cover the building blocks of detection and mitigation — including Cloudflare’s Precursor session-based behavioral detection — and dive into advanced strategies like AI Labyrinth, random action mitigation, and intelligent queuing to protect both origin compute and content integrity.

sessions.title: Breaking the Internet (and putting it back together)
sessions.desc: When you operate a global network, incidents are not just engineering problems, they are coordination, communication, debugging, and trust problems happening under pressure. This session is for infrastructure, SRE, security, and engineering leaders who want a practical look at how Cloudflare manages incidents at scale. Learn how our response process has evolved over the past year, including how AI-assisted tools help teams find signal faster, summarize context, reduce toil, and improve post-incident learning.

sessions.title: Building an open agentic Internet: Discoverable, callable, and payable
sessions.desc: Agents are a new kind of visitor. They don’t render your CSS or click your ads, but there’s a paying human on the other end of every request — block them and you block your customer. Today, billions of those requests are bots re-fetching pages that haven’t changed, which is machine effort with no outcome for either side. This talk lays out the four primitives of a web reshaped around this visitor — readable, discoverable, callable, and payable — plus the identity layer underneath and why they have to be built on open standards. How agents read, discover, call, and pay will decide whether the Internet stays open or whether a handful of stacks own discovery, identity, and payments and everyone else routes through them.

sessions.title: Cloudflare’s Red Team: A story of weaponizing your “won’t fix” backlog
sessions.desc: This talk explains how Cloudflare uses red teaming to stay secure. Learn about the basics of what red teaming is and how it works specifically at Cloudflare. Discover why seemingly minor, low-severity bugs are actually critical, as they are often chained together by attackers to cause major breaches. Then, learn why Cloudflare’s Red Team builds custom command and control (C2) implants and how all these components come together during a live exercise. Finally, hear about the actual outcomes and lessons we learned to help you better protect your own environment.

sessions.title: Convergence: Emerging tech, force amplifiers, and the road ahead
sessions.desc: The leading-edge technologies of today (and tomorrow) aren’t just capabilities in their own right but force amplifiers for other use cases, both good and bad. Every new capability carries within it a new risk, and when you point amplifying technologies at each other, you can end up with unpredictable and exponential outcomes. Come hear how we can collectively employ second-order thinking in the creation of guardrails against future risk and think more broadly about not just what’s possible but how to be ready when it goes wrong. This session is sponsored by Accenture.

speakers.name: Scott Francis
speakers.title: Global BD Lead, Emerging Tech Security

sessions.title: Ferrisway: Ramp’s global routing layer on Cloudflare
sessions.desc: Ferrisway is a Cloudflare Worker that serves as Ramp’s global routing layer, handling 100% of production traffic since January — including API requests, authorizations, webhooks, and AI-driven operations such as agent workflows and MCP tool traffic. It routes about half a billion requests each day, averages more than 5,000 requests per second, and processes roughly 10 TB of traffic daily. In this session, learn how Ferrisway makes fast edge routing decisions from cached configuration, while Gother — its cloud-deployed counterpart — provides a reliable source of truth on cache misses. See how Tail Worker–powered tracing maps Cloudflare execution to Gother spans for end-to-end visibility, how zero-traffic and forced-traffic testing make Worker rollouts safe, and how indirect mappings and explicit unresolved-destination behavior create a consistent, resilient routing layer at global scale.

sessions.title: Financial services panel: Resilience, security, and AI
sessions.desc: Join fellow finance leaders and innovators at our exclusive industry meetup. Connect with peers, share insights, and hear how Cloudflare is helping financial institutions secure applications, harness AI, and optimize performance. Don't miss this opportunity to learn, network, and shape the future of digital finance together.

sessions.title: Getting your storefront agent ready for peak season
sessions.desc: AI agents are reshaping how consumers discover, compare, and buy — and most retail storefronts weren't built for them. Over half of web traffic is already non-human, and early data shows AI-driven retail visits convert at significantly higher rates. Yet most ecommerce teams have no visibility into how agents experience their site or whether they're being recommended at all. This panel session is designed for digital commerce leaders preparing for peak season in an agent-first world. Learn how to measure how AI agents see your brand today, give agents structured ways to interact with your catalog, and evaluate whether to build your own shopping agents — with a clear framework for turning agentic traffic into a channel advantage.

sessions.title: How to get started on your FedRAMP journey with Cloudflare
sessions.desc: Learn how to get started on your FedRAMP Moderate and FedRAMP High journey with Cloudflare in this interactive panel featuring Cloudflare’s Jake Schaeufele, Senior FedRAMP Compliance Specialist, and Tom Lianza, VP of Engineering. Going deep into the architecture, learn how Cloudflare’s developer platform accelerated our roadmap and enabled us to achieve FedRAMP High in under two years. Hear about our lessons learned, alongside real-world advice to help you along your path to FedRAMP status with Cloudflare.

sessions.title: Inside healthcare: Securing and scaling enterprise networks with AI
sessions.desc: Designed for technology leaders in healthcare, this showcase explores how to secure and scale infrastructure using AI. Regulated industries face complex challenges, from sophisticated application programming interface (API) vulnerabilities to hyper-volumetric, distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks. Hear from industry peers on how they’re solving these threats and adding value with emerging technologies.

speakers.name: Jason Shrack
speakers.title: Vice President of Platform Engineering & Services

sessions.title: Scaling Discord’s voice on Cloudflare’s edge
sessions.desc: Moving Discord’s voice and video onto Cloudflare took the migration well beyond a typical rollout. This session takes you through that migration. Hear how we were able to hold the reliability bar by partnering directly with Cloudflare’s engineering teams and working down to the kernel level to understand behavior neither team had mapped before. That collaboration led to fixes on both sides of the stack and changes from Cloudflare that carry forward to other customers running similar workloads. Today, Cloudflare carries more than half of Discord’s voice and video traffic, with quality improving in roughly 70% of migrated regions, pings down more than 30%, and packet loss down 20–60% in multiple regions.

sessions.title: System Sketch — Building Cloudflare on Cloudflare
sessions.desc: Cloudflare builds its own products on the same platform we offer customers — Workers, Workflows, Durable Objects, and Containers. This session is an open discussion about what that looks like in practice: how small teams ship features globally, how they reduce operational burden without servers to patch, and where the trade-offs show up. We walk through real architectural patterns and open the floor to your questions. This session is designed for developers, platform engineers, and architects curious about building on these primitives at scale. Leave with a concrete picture of how Cloudflare uses its own platform to move fast — and how you can, too.

sessions.title: System Sketch — Building EmDash: 10 months of AI, what worked, what broke, what changed
sessions.desc: EmDash is a serverless, AI-native CMS built on Astro and Cloudflare Workers. It began in February 2026 as a one-person project to rebuild WordPress in 60 days. 10 months later, more than 100 people have contributed, and a small maintainer team uses many AI agents and tools to keep up with issues and pull requests, tests, documentation, and releases. This session covers the early challenges, the lessons learned, and how the team’s use of AI changed as the tools improved. You’ll leave with a realistic view of 10 months of AI-assisted open source development, mistakes and all.

sessions.title: System Sketch — Understanding and architecting Cloudflare on-ramps and off-ramps
sessions.desc: As enterprise networks migrate critical workloads to the cloud and adopt autonomous agentic workflows, choosing the right architecture to connect private infrastructure to Cloudflare’s global network is a critical decision. This session provides network architects and IT professionals with a comprehensive, source-grounded guide to evaluating and selecting Cloudflare’s primary connectivity on-ramps: IPsec, Cloudflare Network Interconnect (CNI), and the next-generation Cloudflare Mesh.

sessions.title: The MonkCast from RedMonk: Connect recap
sessions.desc: Join RedMonk, the developer-focused industry analyst firm, for a wrap-up discussion capturing the major themes, product announcements, and key takeaways from Cloudflare Connect 2026. Analysts James Governor and Kate Holterhoff sit down for a live recording of The MonkCast, RedMonk’s podcast capturing the candid, off-script “hallway track” of the tech industry. Together, they unpack the biggest news from across the event — synthesizing how developer platforms, edge computing, and AI capabilities are evolving, and what these shifts mean for practitioners in the field. Geared toward platform engineers, DevRel leaders, infrastructure architects, and technical decision-makers, this conversation offers independent analyst perspective and practical analysis on where the developer ecosystem is heading next.

sessions.title: Accelerate governance, security, and cost control with AI Gateway
sessions.desc: Cloudflare AI Gateway can help enterprises accelerate governance, strengthen data protection, improve resilience, and control cost as AI usage scales across the business. Join Cloudflare for a session on how AI Gateway brings visibility and policy to AI traffic, helps teams manage sensitive data interactions, and provides the operational controls needed to support safe, reliable adoption. See how the right architecture can reduce risk without creating friction, while also giving teams the tools to understand usage, enforce standards, and manage spend as AI becomes embedded in everyday workflows. This session is aimed at practitioners looking for a practical, deployable approach to AI governance and control.

speakers.name: Chelsee Purvis
speakers.title: Senior Cloudflare One Specialist Solutions Engineer

sessions.title: Build It — Deploy AI safely with Cloudflare (repeat)
sessions.desc: Get hands-on with Cloudflare to safely adopt AI across your workforce and applications. In this session, learn how to discover shadow AI usage, steer employees toward approved AI tools, and prevent sensitive data from being shared with public AI services. Then, explore how the same zero trust controls extend to privately deployed AI tools and agents using Cloudflare AI Gateway and DLP profiles to help secure AI traffic, giving teams the visibility, policy enforcement, and data protection they need to move quickly with AI. You must bring your laptop to participate in this session.

sessions.title: Build It — Protect your internal or external AI- or LLM-powered apps now
sessions.desc: As application functionalities increasingly become AI- or LLM-powered to enhance the end user experience, signature-based security falls short. To maintain the same security standard, novel approaches are required. This interactive session showcases various real-life AI/LLM application examples and how to define security rules to guard each of them. The ultimate goal is top-notch security that does not need to slow down innovations. You must bring your laptop to participate in this session.

sessions.title: Build It — Workers Preview: Isolated environments for every change your agent makes (repeat)
sessions.desc: Cloudflare Workers Preview gives every branch a production-like place to run before it ships — its own URL, configuration, bindings, logs, traces, and state — isolated from production and every other change you make. In this hands-on session, you’ll define the starting point every preview branches from and then give one preview its own D1 database or R2 bucket to test configuration and resource changes safely. You’ll leave with a running preview URL and a pre-production feedback loop for agents and humans: deploy, test real behavior, inspect what happened, and verify fixes before they reach production. You must bring your laptop to participate in this session.

sessions.title: Building a software factory: Driving Astro's Issues to zero
sessions.desc: Open source maintainers are burning out under the volume of AI-generated issues and PRs. The Astro team built an automated triage pipeline using isolated AI subagents running inside GitHub Actions. The system reads incoming bug reports, reproduces them in sandboxes, diagnoses root causes, and ships preview releases for reporters to verify. The result: open issues dropped from more than 200 to about 30 — heading toward 0 for the first time in the project's more than 5-year history. This talk covers the architecture behind the pipeline, the state machine driven by issue labels, how we decoupled the logic into a reusable GitHub Action, and the broader lessons about using agent automation to free maintainers to focus on the framework instead of the backlog.

sessions.title: Google and Cloudflare: Turn first-party data into your competitive edge
sessions.desc: Your first-party data is your brand’s biggest competitive advantage. Combining your data with the AI powering Google Ads allows you to find your best customers and drive real business growth. Join Google and Cloudflare to learn how Google tag gateway helps you grow your business by serving tags natively from your own domain, all with a simple setup. Discover how businesses achieve an average 14% increase in observed conversions and lower acquisition costs, and then see a live demonstration showing how simple it is to activate directly in Cloudflare with zero code changes. This session is sponsored by Google.

sessions.title: Better visibility and control: Shining a light on shadow AI
sessions.desc: Blocking AI traffic on day one is a fast way to lose user trust and drive work into the shadows. This session shows how security teams can discover AI and MCP prompts automatically, run DLP in a non-blocking observation mode, measure what would be caught, and tune detection with context before enforcement. Leave this session with a rollout sequence that treats AI security and data protection as an adoption enabler rather than a binary block-or-allow decision.

sessions.title: Bring your own logic with a fully programmable, secure web gateway
sessions.desc: A fixed catalog of AI controls cannot anticipate every customer workflow, model, or risk signal. This session demonstrates how teams can extend Cloudflare Gateway policy with custom selectors and Cloudflare Workers invocations to build organization-specific AI guardrails. The walkthrough covers a practical pattern: detect AI or MCP traffic, evaluate customer context, take a policy action, and use reusable components so the control can be applied consistently. The focus is on empowering security and platform teams to adapt without waiting for a product release.

sessions.title: Building multi-cloud resilience: It starts with DNS
sessions.desc: Modern enterprise infrastructure and operations leaders face a critical architectural challenge: decoupling the global routing control plane from the cloud environment. When multi-cloud strategies rely on provider-specific ingress tools, they risk inheriting cross-cloud dependencies that can fail during widespread outages. This session explores how to build a resilient cloud architecture utilizing a vendor-neutral global edge network to govern traffic before it hits a cloud provider. Learn about the critical points where multi-vendor strategies often fail and how to design around them to suit your specific uptime needs without over-engineering or inflating costs.

sessions.title: From chaos to control: Building a harness for personal agents
sessions.desc: Late last year, we got a taste of what a personal AI agent can look like. You can give it access to your calendar, email, and to-do list and let the agent handle the boring tasks for you. The harness worked, until it didn’t. In this talk, I'll share the architecture of the harness I built for my personal agent that lives on the edge. You’ll get to see the harness that separates demo from production: sub-agents, memory, sandboxing, and human in the loop. Then, I'll share the real issues I ran into during development and the architectural decisions I made to overcome them.

sessions.title: Generative media’s breakthrough moment: Insights from Runway
sessions.desc: Video models have crossed a threshold. What was a novelty one year ago is now reliable enough to sit inside real production workflows — a shift that looks a lot like the moment code generation went from autocomplete to a Claude Code session. In this talk, Runway Chief Product Officer Anthony Maggio traces how video and world models evolved to this point, why generative media is having its own step-change moment, and what that has meant for building the Runway Agent and Runway Dev. Leave with a clearer picture of where generative media is heading and what it takes to turn a fast-moving model capability into a product people actually use.

sessions.title: Internal DNS: The end of the appliance era
sessions.desc: Your public DNS lives on Cloudflare’s global network. Your internal DNS lives in a closet. That gap costs you in three ways: latency from regional appliances, complexity from running two DNS stacks, and risk from infrastructure patched twice a year. Legacy on-premises DNS was never designed for the network you run today. Internal DNS puts authoritative and recursive resolution for private namespaces on the same anycast platform that powers 1.1.1.1: sub-5-second propagation, identity-aware resolution through Cloudflare Gateway. This demo session covers the architecture, looks at real customer migrations off legacy DNS, and explores what closing the gap unlocks.

sessions.title: Oracle and Cloudflare: Building a stronger foundation for enterprise innovation
sessions.desc: What becomes possible when two enterprise technology leaders combine their strengths? In this session, executives from Cloudflare and Oracle explore their partnership and its potential to help organizations around the world simplify, secure, and accelerate their digital operations. The conversation looks at the complementary capabilities of both companies, the customer needs driving the collaboration, and how the partnership can give businesses a stronger foundation for their applications, data, and future innovation. This session is sponsored by Oracle.

sessions.title: Poisoning the well: The rise of indirect prompt injection in the agentic age
sessions.desc: As we shift from simple chatbots to autonomous AI agents that can browse the web, manage our calendars, and even audit our code, we have inadvertently opened a back door for a new breed of silent adversary. Indirect prompt injection (IDPI) allows attackers to weaponize the very data your AI consumes — turning a routine web search or an incoming support ticket into a remote instruction that can exfiltrate sensitive data or hijack tool execution. This session explores how attackers are seeding the open web with malicious payloads designed specifically to compromise the “lethal trifecta” of private data access, tool execution, and inherent reasoning gaps in LLMs. We will map out the increasingly hostile landscape of the agentic era.

sessions.title: Protecting AI agents with Cloudflare One
sessions.desc: AI agents are proliferating inside enterprise networks with static API keys and no identity checks. This session deconstructs how Cloudflare One treats agents as first-class identities at the edge.  Explore machine-to-machine authentication via Access service tokens, short-lived mTLS, and ZTNA segmentation enforcing least privilege without network complexity. Also, learn how you can use Cloudflare Gateway to inspect agent-to-SaaS traffic in real time and DLP policies to prevent exfiltration. The outcome: a concrete architecture that replaces secret sprawl with policy-driven enforcement.

sessions.title: System Sketch — Building agentic apps on Workers: A case study with Cloudflare OS
sessions.desc: What does it look like to build a real agentic application on Cloudflare Workers? In this interactive session, we'll whiteboard Cloudflare OS, an internal AI productivity tool, as a case study. We'll map Dynamic Workers for cheap compute, Workers Durable Objects Facets for isolation and state, Code Mode for RPC-based agent-to-app interaction, and gatekeeper patterns for secure egress. Designed for developers and architects, this session outlines the trade-offs of autonomous execution. Leave with a concrete reference architecture and a clear blueprint of which primitives to reach for when building your own.

sessions.title: System Sketch — Protecting the inside user: AI governance, prompt inspection, and leakage
sessions.desc: As internal teams rapidly integrate generative AI into their workflows, security teams are left asking, “What sensitive data is leaving our network, and what unvetted content is coming back in?” Join this session for an interactive, hands-on whiteboard session to learn how to secure employee AI interactions and eliminate data exposure risks using Cloudflare Guardrails for AI.

speakers.name: Bob Perciaccante
speakers.title: Senior Cloudflare One Specialist Solutions Engineer

sessions.title: System Sketch — Real-world infrastructure patterns for vibe coding workloads
sessions.desc: Vibe coding workloads — autonomous agents writing, running, and deploying code — demand a different infrastructure than traditional apps. This session, designed for platform engineers and architects supporting AI coding agents, shares real-world experience from building these workloads across multiple customers on Cloudflare. We’ll whiteboard the architecture: sandboxes for isolated code execution, egress control for credential safety, Durable Objects for session coordination, and the performance and security trade-offs we hit in production. Leave with a reference architecture battle-tested across real deployments and the pitfalls to avoid.

sessions.title: The prompt is lava
sessions.desc: Sentry, by its nature, needs to ingest untrusted telemetry on behalf of our customers. With the growing number of customers using MCP, and local agents to debug Sentry issues, the prompt injection through telemetry is a real vector of attack. Hear about this specific problem and economical ways to control the issue.

sessions.title: Security vs. reach: Who controls your AI visibility?
sessions.desc: Security teams own the Cloudflare settings that decide which bots reach a company’s website. Marketing teams feel the result when an AI assistant stops citing their announcements. Shashi Bellamkonda of Info-Tech Research Group talks with Bryan Becker, Director of Product Management for Fraud and Web Integrity at Cloudflare, about two sides of that problem. One is how sites can stay in search while refusing AI training. The other is how to make pages readable for the assistants that fetch them for live answers.

sessions.title: Behind the scenes: Challenges of running AI models at scale
sessions.desc: Cloudflare runs at a massive scale — but what does scale mean when it comes to running AI models? We can talk about scale in different dimensions: global scale (routing, autoscaling, and concurrency), model catalog scale (breadth and modalities of models), and even model scale (trillion+ parameter models). Cloudflare does all of the above. Join this session for a behind-the-scenes look at the systems behind Workers AI infrastructure and how we operate them.

sessions.title: Building secure, composable agents with Flue
sessions.desc: AI agents do not behave like traditional applications: they choose tools dynamically, cross trust boundaries, and must adapt while they run. This session is for developers building real-world agentic systems. Using Flue, we show how hooks, composable capabilities, and Cloudflare Workers bindings can make agents flexible without giving up control. A live demo traces an agent through a multi-step workflow, showing where policies are enforced. Leave with patterns for designing trust boundaries, adding guardrails where models act, and assembling reusable agent building blocks.

speakers.name: Fred Schott
speakers.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Creator of Astro

sessions.title: Cloudflare’s evolution of managing IP addresses for customers at scale
sessions.desc: Learn about the ways Cloudflare ensures reliability, performance, and global reachability for its customers’ websites, domains, and their users. Contrary to the design of IP, addresses are often tied to domain names and applications in ways that stifle innovation and even cause incidents. However, in 2021, Cloudflare announced trials and technology to decouple names from addresses. In 2024, Cloudflare revealed new technology to manage addresses dynamically and safely and disseminate changes globally, in just seconds. Cloudflare is now using its knowledge and technology to better scale with the Internet and to help advance the evolution of IP addresses. (Note: this does not apply to BYOIP, static, and dedicated addressing.)

sessions.title: Code Mode: Fit 2,500 API endpoints into 1,000 tokens
sessions.desc: MCP promises to be the USB port for AI agents, but every tool consumes tokens. Cloudflare’s API has 2,500 endpoints; exposing them all would eat 1.17 million tokens, exceeding any model’s context window. We built Code Mode, an open source technique that collapses any number of tools into 2 functions and roughly 1,000 tokens, a 99.9% reduction. Agents write JavaScript to query OpenAPI specs and call endpoints on demand inside sandboxed V8 isolates where credentials never touch the model. In this talk, see production numbers from our internal deployment and leave with the SDK to implement this on your own MCP servers today.

sessions.title: Don't block shadow AI on campus. Out-design it.
sessions.desc: Conventional shadow AI controls do not survive contact with university governance, and FERPA exposure grows daily. There is a different answer: stop treating the campus network as an enforcement point and start treating it as a strategic platform. When on-campus AI unlocks institutional context (degree audits, LMS, scheduling, and ERPs) that off-campus AI cannot reach, students and faculty seek the network out. Governance follows naturally. In this session for higher education CIOs and IT leaders, a Cloudflare SE and a higher education technology leader share a deployable reference architecture, discuss the framing to socialize it internally, and provide a live demo.

speakers.name: Michael Hacker
speakers.title: Associate Vice President for Strategy, Transformation, and Innovation (AI)

sessions.title: From the endpoint to the edge: Simplifying security in the AI era
sessions.desc: Environmental complexity is growing. At the same time, attacks are getting faster, more complex, and coming from more directions then ever. Learn how SentinelOne and Cloudflare have partnered to deliver integrations and solutions to help bring enterprise-class automation, network security, and endpoint intelligence and response to any organization. See how Cloudflare’s SASE and zero trust services combine with SentinelOne’s Autonomous Security Intelligence platform to address real scenarios and attacks organizations are facing today. This demo session is sponsored by SentinelOne.

speakers.name: Tyler Greenfield
speakers.title: Senior Manager AMER Channel Partner Solutions Engineering

sessions.title: How to manage Cloudflare at scale without overwhelm
sessions.desc: Managing Cloudflare for a big organization can be overwhelming. How do you give users the right blend of autonomy and compliance? How do you make sure that you’re setting yourself up for success around cost, permissions, and reliability? This session gives you the basics for how to set your organization up for success using all the latest innovations from Cloudflare.

sessions.title: How we built Command Code, the most used open-model harness, at 950T tokens
sessions.desc: How did Command Code make DeepSeek outperform Claude Opus with tool repair harness engineering research? Now at 950 trillion–token scale and over 100K developers, Command Code is fixing billions of tokens for open models. A couple of months ago, developers did not trust open models. Bounced tool calls, wasted context, and poor cache hit ratios made capable models look broken. We purpose-built a coding agent harness for open models: a repair layer that fixes malformed tool calls, a taste model that learns your coding preferences, and per-provider cache pinning that holds a 99.43% cache hit rate at trillions of tokens per day. In this talk, learn how you can cut your AI costs by 10 to 20 times while also increasing the amount of work done using an abundance of tokens with top open models.

sessions.title: Into the tunnel: Secure, metadata-driven routing at scale
sessions.desc: Cloudflare Tunnels aren’t just for secure access. We use them to load-balance traffic into our AWS-powered network, at scale, across every hostname in our zone. No open ports. Just secure, distributed traffic flowing exactly where it needs to go. We pushed Tunnels and Cloudflare for SaaS past their expected limits, combining them with metadata in ways that got creative fast. In this session, see how we built smarter, more flexible routing out of that combination. Learn about the real problems we hit, the workarounds we tried, and the approach that finally stuck. You’ll leave with practical patterns you can apply to your own multi-tenant or SaaS routing setup, no matter how messy your infrastructure already is.

sessions.title: No one defends alone: CISA and industry against nation-state threats
sessions.desc: Nation-state actors are pre-positioning in American critical infrastructure at a scale no single organization can see or stop alone. CISA's Joint Cyber Defense Collaborative exists for this moment: to fuse government intelligence with private sector visibility into a unified defense posture. This session puts CISA's Chief of Industry Partnerships in conversation with Cloudflare to examine what coordinated public-private defense looks like in practice — how AI-assisted adversary operations are forcing real-time adaptation of shared defenses, which critical infrastructure sectors face the most acute exposure right now, and what makes coordinated disruption operations against PRC and nation-state threats work — and where they fall short.

sessions.title: Prevent cloud misconfigurations and data leakage before they happen
sessions.desc: Cloud Workload Security is a new and unique approach to securing cloud resources. While most tools focus on catching risks after the fact, CWS uses an inline proxy to inspect cloud API calls as they happen. It enforces policy as code in real time, blocking insecure or unapproved actions before the cloud provider ever executes them, both at creation and during runtime. The CWS policy engine lets teams enforce controls that weren’t practically possible before. In this session, we walk through two examples: preventing data exfiltration to untrusted external accounts in AWS, and then securing the configuration and runtime of AI services like Amazon Bedrock. Leave understanding how to prevent cloud risks with CWS.

sessions.title: Build It — Agent-first development on Cloudflare (repeat)
sessions.desc: In this hands-on session, set up your coding agent for Cloudflare development using Cloudflare Skills and MCP and then use it to build and deploy a real Worker with a bound KV namespace. We cover how to use Skills effectively, deploy via temporary accounts, and work the agent feedback loop — deploy, verify, read errors, fix, redeploy — until it’s live. Leave with your agent configured, a deployed Worker, and a repeatable workflow for Cloudflare development. You must bring your laptop and to participate in this session.

sessions.title: Build It — Build durable AI agents with Flue on Cloudflare (repeat)
sessions.desc: In this hands-on session, build and deploy a durable AI agent using the Flue Framework on Cloudflare Workers. Starting from scratch, create an agent, give it tools to call external APIs, add a sub-agent for delegation, and deploy it live — all powered by Cloudflare Workers Durable Objects for persistence and recovery. We cover the Flue hook model, sandbox strategies, and the deploy-test-iterate loop. Leave with a working agent and patterns to build more. This session is designed for developers and system architects looking to orchestrate reliable AI workflows. You must bring your laptop to participate in this session.

sessions.title: Credentials without secrets: Unforgeable access for Workers
sessions.desc: Service credentials are annoying to set up, hard to prevent from leaking, and painful to rotate when they leak anyway. In this talk, preview an approach that allows Cloudflare Workers to identify themselves and call protected resources using capabilities that are unforgeable live objects rather than leakable secrets. See how this model applies to zero trust access, and hear why capability-based security uniquely suits the variety and pace demanded by AI agents. Then, explore composition and delegation, or what it means to combine credentials, pass them around, and act on behalf of another.

sessions.title: Rise of the agents: How Cloudflare detects, defends & responds at AI speed
sessions.desc: What if your security systems didn’t just alert you — they also acted? At Cloudflare, we’re building agentic AI into every phase of security operations. This session covers how we use AI to automate the routine, accelerate incident response from hours to minutes, and augment engineer judgment on the alerts that actually matter. Walk through what we’ve built and what’s running in production today — from automated behavioral alert triage that contacts employees directly and assesses their responses without engineer involvement, to AI systems that open and enrich every security ticket before a human arrives and an engineer-facing assistant that connects to every tool we use and compresses hours of investigation work into seconds. From architecture and automation frameworks to real lessons from running AI in production, this session is a practitioner’s look at operationalizing agentic AI in security — how we built it, how we adopted it, and how we’re doing it safely.

sessions.title: System Sketch — This is my workflow: Building with AI
sessions.desc: Everyone's talking about AI-assisted development, but what does it actually look like day to day? This interactive session is designed for developers using or exploring AI in their daily workflow. A Cloudflare engineer will walk through their real workflow — the tools they use, how they structure prompts, where AI helps most, and where it still falls short. We'll cover practical tips and patterns you can take back to your own work and then open the floor to compare notes. Leave with concrete techniques and a clearer picture of what works today.

sessions.title: An agent that onboards a photography studio — on Workers AI
sessions.desc: Photography studios pay for VSCO Workspace and deserve a premium onboarding experience. Onboarding used to be a checklist; now an agent handles the setup. This talk explores the production agent that guides a new studio from lead to payment, creating jobs and quotes against a live API with checkpoints, authentication, and evaluation. The agent brain runs on Cloudflare Workers AI; learn why we compared Gemma and GLM on the same harness and kept every write behind step-order gates. Leave this talk with the architecture and insights into where Workers AI excelled and the gaps still open (minute-long turns, no user-facing stream, and whether Durable Objects belong at the edge).

sessions.title: Application services for private origins: Today’s patterns and what’s next
sessions.desc: Enterprises run critical applications on private origins: behind firewalls, in VPCs, and across hybrid clouds. These apps lack the same edge protection as their public-facing counterparts, so organizations maintain costly appliances like F5 BIG-IP or build complex hairpin architectures to compensate. Cloudflare application services for private networks extend Cloudflare’s WAF, DDoS, load balancing, and bot management to private origins — traffic reaches origins through Cloudflare Tunnel, Cloudflare WAN, IPsec, or Cloudflare Network Interconnect (CNI). This session walks through the patterns customers deploy today, real production examples, and the roadmap for unifying public and private application security.

sessions.title: Automating app development the secure way: Velocity meets defense in depth
sessions.desc: AI coding assistants have fundamentally transformed developer velocity. Today, developers can describe an app in plain English and deploy it to Cloudflare's global network in minutes. How do engineering teams keep that speed while ensuring every app is ready for real users and data? This session demonstrates a repeatable pattern for building on the Cloudflare Developer Platform with the AI coding tools developers already use. Explore deploying applications on Cloudflare using natural language within platform-enforced guardrails, and then see it automatically inherit your organization's defense-in-depth baseline.

sessions.title: Disrupting scam and fraud networks with armies of AI agents on Cloudflare
sessions.desc: Scams and fraud are run as businesses, and often their defenders can only react once the money has moved. Apate gets there first. In this session, hear how Apate uses thousands of AI agents to engage scammers across chat, WhatsApp, Telegram, email, and voice, participating in hundreds of thousands of messages and calls per day. See how agents can reach victims mid-scam, before the payment leaves.

sessions.title: Ensuring resiliency during network maintenance
sessions.desc: Designed for network and infrastructure leaders, this session explores how Cloudflare maintains resiliency and data integrity while expanding our massive global footprint. Upgrading a rapidly growing network requires rigorous risk analysis and scheduling algorithms to maintain seamless operations. Learn how our engineering teams tackle this issue by replaying historical data via backtesting to prevent recurring issues and by coordinating capacity increases and maintenance schedules. We also share how our stateful edge products, such as Cloudflare R2 Storage, use maintenance-aware placement to automatically rebalance workloads to ensure availability and performance during major hardware migrations. Join us to learn how our infrastructure investments translate into a more resilient platform for your workloads.

sessions.title: Hono: Web application primitives for the AI era
sessions.desc: Modern AI agents and full-stack frameworks need more than agents, content, or UIs. They need web application primitives: routing, middleware, request context, streaming, and runtime portability. In this lightning talk, learn how Hono is used by or integrated into tools and frameworks like Astro, Flue, Mastra, and Void; how you can use Hono within those frameworks; and how to apply the same web layer pattern in your own applications. Also learn how to structure agent endpoints, compose middleware for auth and validation, and design HTTP interfaces that can run across Cloudflare Workers, Node.js, Bun, and Deno.

sessions.title: Inside the global effort to disrupt advanced phishing operations
sessions.desc: In 2025 and 2026, Cloudflare and Microsoft collaborated with global public and private partners to disrupt multiple advanced phishing-as-a-service operations involving the theft of thousands of victims’ login credentials, which were then used to facilitate financial crimes such as business email compromise. This session covers the technical aspects of identifying the criminal infrastructure and the conspirators as well as the legal process to coordinate shutting it all down. Learn about information sharing, how to report abuse, and how Cloudflare and Microsoft are working together to help build a better Internet.

speakers.name: Brian Carter
speakers.title: Threat Research Director – Cybercrime, Cloudforce One – PREDICT

sessions.title: Protecting web and API applications from AI-powered attacks
sessions.desc: AI is making it faster and cheaper to discover vulnerabilities, generate attack variants, and evade traditional defenses. Learn how you can layer managed rules and WAF attack score to protect applications against known threats and novel variations. Explore how Cloudflare proactively tests these defenses with adaptive LLM agents, turning discovered gaps into stronger protections. Finally, look ahead to better detection models and an automated feedback loop that continuously converts new attack techniques into defenses for customers.

sessions.title: Reducing payloads with shared compression dictionaries
sessions.desc: Modern web applications ship repeated patterns across JavaScript, CSS, APIs, and page responses, but traditional compression treats many of those responses independently. This problem is more pronounced in the vibe-coding era. In this session, developers, platform teams, and performance engineers can learn to make sites faster while reducing bandwidth costs. Learn how shared compression dictionaries work, where they help most, and how you can deploy them safely through Cloudflare. You will leave with a practical model for identifying dictionary-friendly traffic, measuring performance impact, and rolling out compression improvements without changing application code.

sessions.title: The agentic network: Secure private connectivity for agents
sessions.desc: AI agents can’t use VPN clients or type MFA codes, so every agentic workflow breaks at the same point: the agent needs to reach a private database, internal API, or MCP server. Exposing those resources publicly is a security risk, and legacy VPNs grant too much access and leave no audit trail. In this demo session, see how Cloudflare Mesh becomes the universal connectivity fabric for the agentic era. We’ll build three secure patterns from scratch in five minutes each: a coding agent reaching a private database, a Worker using a VPC binding to fetch from an internal API, and bidirectional node-to-node mesh across different cloud providers. See how every connection inherits Cloudflare One Gateway policies and DLP automatically with no extra setup.

sessions.title: Turning data questions into data infra with Cloudflare Basin
sessions.desc: Business, product, and go-to-market leaders have questions about what is happening in their businesses. This usually involves teams of engineers instrumenting systems, capturing and processing events, building data pipelines, and managing data infra. What if we could go in the other direction — ask the question, and then use agents to generate all of the infrastructure needed to answer it? This is the agentic future we built for with Cloudflare Basin. In this session, learn what Basin is, how it works, and how anyone — from developers to executives — can build their company’s data infra on it.

sessions.title: Attacker-perspective findings from real-world WAF deployments
sessions.desc: WAFs are one of the most effective controls security teams have — when they’re deployed, configured, and continuously validated the way they’re meant to be. The challenge most teams face isn’t the technology; it’s visibility into how that technology is actually performing in production, at scale, over time. That’s the question IONIX set out to answer with their State of the WAF Report, built on attacker-perspective probing of real-world WAF deployments across their external attack surface customer base. The findings reveal where the gap between deployment and full enforcement tends to open: coverage that isn’t yet mapped, policies still in learning mode, and configuration drift that goes unnoticed without ongoing validation. Join IONIX CTO Billy Hoffman as he shares the report’s key findings and what continuous validation looks like in practice for a strong WAF program. This session is sponsored by IONIX.

sessions.title: Replacing a third-party IdP with Cloudflare Access, authentik, and OPA
sessions.desc: Security and identity teams depend on identity providers (IdPs) to protect every internal app, but a vendor compromise can turn that dependency into supply chain risk. This session is for security leaders, identity engineers, and zero trust architects. See how Cloudflare replaced our third-party IdP with Cloudflare’s Access for SaaS and OPA/Rego. Learn how to protect identity from supply chain attacks, run an IdP migration, and add fail-safes when identity becomes code.

sessions.title: Application Security Associate certification exam
sessions.desc: The Cloudflare Application Security Associate certification gives customers, partners, and practitioners formal proof of their Cloudflare AppSec expertise, strengthening hiring decisions, accelerating product adoption, and reducing misconfiguration risk in production. This proctored exam session — designed for security professionals, developers, and administrators with hands-on Cloudflare experience — covers WAF, DDoS, bot management, API security, and analytics. Leave with an industry-recognized Cloudflare credential, a Credly badge, and the validation of practical AppSec skills.

sessions.title: Zero Trust Associate certification exam
sessions.desc: The Cloudflare Zero Trust Associate certification validates the skills practitioners need to move organizations off legacy VPNs and onto modern ZTNA, addressing one of the most urgent transitions in enterprise security today. This proctored exam session — designed for security analysts, network engineers, and partner SEs with one to two years of hands-on experience — covers zero trust concepts, identity, the Cloudflare One Client, Cloudflare Tunnel connectors, traffic policies, and Cloudflare Access. Gain a recognized Cloudflare credential and a Credly badge as well as confidence implementing zero trust on the Cloudflare One platform for clients or your own organization.

sessions.title: Auto model routing saves money, makes users happy, and is inherently flawed
sessions.desc: Cloudflare AI Gateway includes an automatic model router that can reduce AI spending without reducing productivity. This talk walks through the router architecture that was built for performance, interpretability, and adaptability. But despite its obvious benefits, is automatic model routing actually a good idea, or are there smarter ways to waste less money? This talk explores that question.

sessions.title: Build low-latency pub/sub applications with MoQ
sessions.desc: Developers building real-time applications often choose between media delivery protocols such as HLS and DASH and interactive technologies such as WebRTC. Media over QUIC (MoQ) provides a shared pub/sub model and lets applications tune latency and reliability as conditions change. Learn how MoQ works, when to use it, and how to build with it in browsers and native apps using Cloudflare’s relay and open source tools. Demos will cover live media and other low-latency use cases, from one-to-one communication to large-scale fan-out.

sessions.title: Cloudflare One’s vision for data sovereignty: Cryptography over geography
sessions.desc: Governments worldwide are demanding that data stay within their borders. The industry’s typical solution, which localizes traffic to physical data centers in each region, leads to higher costs, slower performance, reduced resilience, and limited fallback when things go wrong. We think there’s a better way. This session shares Cloudflare One’s vision for using cryptography instead of geography to keep data in region. We walk through our approach to regionalizing key management, traffic inspection, logging, and operations, and where we’re headed with post-quantum cryptography by 2028.

sessions.title: Discovering primitives: Tools you or your agents can use to build the web
sessions.desc: Cloudflare has an ever-expanding set of tools and primitives to power modern web applications, but how do you discover them all and make informed choices about what to use and when? In the age of agentic development, thoughtful technical architecture and software engineering are more important than ever. In this session, explore the Cloudflare product suite and how it’s designed to power even the most demanding of web applications. See some of the fundamental primitives available as well as some of the newer emerging tools. Then, learn how you can guide your agents to further discover the tools available from Cloudflare and make sound decisions about how to leverage this powerful set of web infrastructure products.

sessions.title: Durable AI workflows with Effect: Maintaining open source at scale
sessions.desc: Every project produces signals that help guide its evolution. Products learn from telemetry, usage, and customer behavior, while open source projects like Effect learn from issues, pull requests, discussions, and contributor feedback. The rise of AI-assisted development dramatically increased the volume of these signals, eventually outpacing our ability to review, interpret, and act on them. To address this problem, we built “The Janitor,” an AI maintainer that reviews incoming issues and pull requests, gathers missing context, organizes related work, and surfaces what needs human attention. We show how running durable workflows with Effect on Cloudflare’s Developer Platform helps us separate signal from noise so maintainers can spend time where it matters most.

sessions.title: From ranking to recommended: Answer engine optimization (AEO)
sessions.desc: Discovery is moving from search rankings to AI recommendations. Customers ask an assistant, and it names a shortlist before anyone visits your site. Unlike search, there's no impression count and no missed-click report, so when a competitor is recommended instead of you, you never find out. This session is for marketers and site owners who want to tackle AI-driven discovery. See how Cloudflare measures how often assistants recommend you against competitors, using realistic customer prompts. Join this session to see your recommendation metrics, find where you're named but not cited, and take action to improve your results.

sessions.title: Hacking AI and why you should run Guardrails on the edge
sessions.desc: Jailbreaking, prompt injection, misalignment, data leakage, biased answers, hallucinations, memory poisoning, wrong behavior... AI is great, but it can also be hacked, abused, or just need to be reinforced by a robust corporate security policy. This session covers hacking techniques for weaknesses and vulnerabilities and covers how you can protect your digital AI service using Guardrails — and why you should do this on the edge with Cloudflare.

sessions.title: I built your personal software ecosystem
sessions.desc: What if you had your own npm registry, your own GitHub, your own cron, your own email address, and your own database? And what if your favorite AI assistant could build with all of it on your behalf? That’s Kody. Every user gets a fully isolated software ecosystem. Your AI writes packages into your own Git repos, publishes to your personal registry, schedules jobs, runs services and workflows, and gets email at your own address. In this session, learn how software engineer and educator Kent C. Dodds built Kody entirely on Cloudflare, the only place it could be built. Dig in to sandboxing AI-authored code with Worker Loaders, per-user Git hosting with Artifacts, namespaced Durable Objects, and wiring D1, R2, Vectorize, Queues, Workflows, and Email Routing into a multi-tenant platform. When AI builds software for everyone, this is what’s underneath. You can start today.

sessions.title: Modern customer security engineering
sessions.desc: This session details how we rebuilt a security-focused production data processing platform on the Cloudflare Developer Platform. Learn about designing an AI-native architecture using the developer platform and building and operating AI-driven processing pipelines in production. Discover how we leveled up our workflows with Cloudflare AI Gateway, and explore coordinating distributed workflows and long-running processes. Additional topics include observability, reliability, and operational lessons learned; what became significantly simpler and what remained challenging; and what we would approach differently if starting again today.

sessions.title: Secure AI at scale: Cloudflare’s vision for trusted AI adoption
sessions.desc: AI adoption is moving faster than most security models can keep up. In this session, Cloudflare shares its vision for helping organizations use AI without losing control of sensitive data, identities, or applications. See how organizations can secure employee use of AI, protect AI-powered applications, and govern autonomous agents at scale. Leave with a practical framework for reducing risk while giving teams room to experiment, build, and deploy AI with confidence.

sessions.title: Transforming the enterprise WAN
sessions.desc: Discover how users leverage Cloudflare WAN with BGP to consolidate and simplify private wide-area networks. This session reveals how Cloudflare WAN solved the routing limitations and operational complexity that traditional solutions couldn’t address.

speakers.name: Naresh Chhetri
speakers.title: Global IT, Global Network Architecture Lead

sessions.title: Your agent wrote it. Who’s on call?
sessions.desc: Cloudflare shipped an OAuth library for Cloudflare Workers largely written by AI, publishing prompts alongside code for the industry to review commit by commit. This provided an early, honest look at what agent-authored production code takes to get right: a lot of review. As generation stops being the bottleneck, the constraint moves downstream — to review, CI, and production, where failures land on on-call engineers who didn’t write the code. This panel examines the data: Factory brings throughput numbers from agentic coding teams; Sentry brings failure profiles — error classes, revert rates, triage time. Is generated code’s distinct failure pattern a generation problem or a review problem?

sessions.title: Red-teaming and defending an AI chatbot live with AI Gateway
sessions.desc: Your team shipped an AI chatbot that users love. Then an attacker asked it to translate its system instructions, dumping every credential and patient record. For security practitioners and platform engineers, this session reveals what breaks and how Cloudflare stops it. Watch as we deploy a healthcare chatbot on Workers AI, red-team it live with OWASP-mapped attacks, and experience a data leak in real time. Then see how we enable AI Gateway Guardrails, DLP, and WAF AI Security for Apps to block prompt injections at the edge. You’ll leave with a clear mental model of AI failures and how to mitigate them.

sessions.title: Validating trust in the AI-accelerated SDLC with Wiz & Cloudflare
sessions.desc: The AI-accelerated SDLC introduces new security and governance challenges, changing the software supply chain trust model. AI agents create unseen areas, exposed endpoints, shadow AI, and data leakage that traditional tools miss. Security teams need full visibility paired with exploitability and runtime context to validate real risk. This session, for security professionals and developers, details how Wiz and Cloudflare deliver unified, end-to-end AI protection. See a live demo and explore a case study to learn about challenges and solutions for scaling application security in an AI world and hear how Wiz’s security platform powers this unique risk-driven approach. This session is sponsored by Wiz.

sessions.title: Build It — Deploy data sovereignty controls with Cloudflare Data Localization Suite
sessions.desc: Need to keep customer data in-region without rebuilding your architecture or losing performance and DDoS protections? Cloudflare Data Localization Suite gives teams practical controls over where Cloudflare processes traffic, stores metadata, and manages cryptographic keys. In this hands-on session, Cloudflare product experts guide attendees through a real-time setup of three core capabilities: Regional Services for regional traffic processing, Customer Metadata Boundary for data storage boundaries, and Geo Key Manager for regional TLS private key management. Configure each product, see which architectures and workloads Cloudflare supports today, and learn how to partner with Cloudflare on data localization requirements after the session. You must bring your laptop to participate in this session.

speakers.name: Erik Engstrom
speakers.title: Product | Data Localization Suite + Cloudflare for SaaS

sessions.title: Build It — Deploy to Void: Launch vibe-coded apps instantly (repeat)
sessions.desc: Agents make building apps easy. Now, deploy them just as easily. In this session, get an exclusive preview of the new Void deployment platform. Upgrade your vibe-coded apps with Cloudflare’s databases, cron jobs, WebSockets, and more. You must bring your laptop to participate in this session.

sessions.title: Build It — Deploy your own AI workspace with Cloudflare OS (repeat)
sessions.desc: Cloudflare OS is an open source AI productivity environment built on Cloudflare Workers. In this hands-on session, deploy your own instance and then customize it with two real changes: configuring a gatekeeper to give your agents safe access to an external service, and writing a custom skill that teaches your agent how your team works. Along the way, learn the architecture — Workers Durable Objects, Dynamic Worker facets, and the gatekeeper security model. Leave with a running, customized instance and the foundation to make it your company’s OS. This session is designed for architects and others working to enable AI productivity at their organizations. You must bring your laptop to participate in this session.

sessions.title: System Sketch — Creating an infinite extensibility layer to your Secure Web Gateway
sessions.desc: Traditional Secure Web Gateways lock security teams into binary choices: allow or block. By embedding Cloudflare Workers directly into Cloudflare Gateway, traffic evaluation shifts from rigid policy toggles to a programmable control plane. Security engineers can now inject custom, context-aware logic in real time — enriching web requests with third-party intelligence, crafting dynamic routing rules, or enforcing bespoke compliance checks on demand. In this session, discover how this infinite extensibility layer transforms the gateway from a passive boundary into an adaptable edge platform, empowering organizations to break free from vendor constraints and programmatically dictate how every byte of secure web traffic is inspected, controlled, and routed.

speakers.name: Giriraj Jayaraman
speakers.title: Principal Cloudflare One Specialist Solutions Engineer

sessions.title: Advertising prefixes for fun and profit: How to anycast
sessions.desc: Cloudflare’s network uses anycast to advertise the same IP prefixes from locations globally, enabling Internet routing to direct traffic toward an available Cloudflare data center. But operating anycast at global scale takes more than announcing a prefix with BGP. This session traces the evolution of prefix advertisements at Cloudflare, from relatively static routing configurations to increasingly automated, adaptive systems. Explore how routing policy, network topology, capacity, health signals, and traffic engineering influence where prefixes are advertised and how incoming traffic is distributed. Learn about operational challenges that shaped this evolution, including uneven traffic, overloaded locations, routing convergence, and the need to make changes safely across a large network. Leave with an intermediate-level understanding of how anycast works, why prefix-advertisement strategies evolve as networks grow, and what it takes to build reliable, efficient global load balancing.

sessions.title: Can we have both data sovereignty and a global Internet?
sessions.desc: The modern Internet is the most global system ever designed by humans. In our rapidly changing world, it must also be highly region-specific to support the needs of regulated customers. How do we keep a global Internet, while also supporting the needs of data sovereignty frameworks globally? For this panel discussion, join Cloudflare’s Chief Legal Officer Alissa Starzak, Head of Global Government Relations Vincent Voci, and Product Leader for Data Sovereignty Wesley Evans, as they discuss the future of the global network and how we plan to keep one Internet.

sessions.title: Canary to cloud: Building a flexible traffic strategy
sessions.desc: Moving from an on-premises stack to cloud environments changes more than where applications run; it changes how traffic must be controlled throughout the transition. In this session, Uber and Cloudflare share how they are modernizing load balancing to route traffic safely between on-premises and cloud environments. Learn how Cloudflare’s flexible traffic controls and custom rules help Uber direct selected traffic to canary environments, validate changes, and expand deployments gradually. We also explore how Uber can rapidly shift traffic between environments as conditions change, reducing operational risk while allowing services to migrate on their own timelines.

sessions.title: Cloudflare’s Red Team: Building AI harnesses that actually work
sessions.desc: AI models are powerful, but they don’t hunt for vulnerabilities on their own. You need a harness, which is the scaffolding that feeds tasks to the models, manages the data, and validates the output. When we first started using AI for security research, we relied on simple skills in interactive CLI sessions. We quickly realized that this doesn’t scale and isn’t sustainable for production environments. In this session, discover how we moved away from simple prompt-based research to a flexible, model-agnostic architecture where models act as interchangeable components. Learn about the safety measures we built to ensure our automated research doesn’t expose customer data or cross security boundaries — including how we use cross-model adversarial validation and automated triage. Finally, see our roadmap for what’s next, specifically how we’re scaling our investigations with in-house classifiers and active monitoring to stay ahead as models become more capable.

sessions.title: Enabling creators worldwide: Scaling Canva on Cloudflare
sessions.desc: Canva is empowering the world to design. With over 260 million monthly active platform users and more than 400 designs created per second globally, Canva relies on trusted partners like Cloudflare to deliver solutions today and co-engineer the future. In this fireside chat for platform architects and engineering leaders, Cloudflare VP of Product Steve Goldsmith, Canva Senior Engineering Manager Michael Yates, and Canva Principal Software Engineer Adam “Laz” Lazur share examples from their joint engineering efforts, with detailed technical explanations and anecdotes from real-world delivery experience at Canva. Leave with concrete insights on balancing security, scale, and high-performance global platform tuning.

sessions.title: From YOLO mode to zero trust: Building an agentic engineering control plane
sessions.desc: Autonomous agents now rapidly write code, patch servers, and operate infrastructure. They can exfiltrate IP or take down production just as fast. The velocity is real; so is the scope of impact. Drawing on Swiss Post’s zero trust program and codeflare.ch, we build the control plane live on one whiteboard. No slides here. We explore Cloudflare AI Gateway for semantic DLP and cost caps, identity lineage tying every agent action to a real engineer, MCP portals cutting tool footprints by up to 99%, and ephemeral sandboxes detonated after every run. The cherry on top is an inference mesh turning idle hardware into a private LLM fabric. No prompt leaves your network, and cost collapses. Leave with a blueprint to deploy tomorrow.

speakers.name: Nikola Novoselec
speakers.title: Technical Director, Agentic AI Architecture & Governance and Zero Trust Program

sessions.title: How to measure real-world network quality for end users
sessions.desc: Speed tests are a common tool for diagnosing poor connections and comparing Internet service providers. But traditional tests often measure performance under ideal conditions, not the real-world experience users actually have. Cloudflare helps customers measure end-user connections in the wild, where network quality really matters. In this session, hear our approach to measuring network quality and learn from the industry leaders at Orb, who are redefining what it means to understand your Internet connection. Also, see a demo of how you can use the Network Quality API to build end-user performance measurements and improve performance for your customers.

sessions.title: Securing agentic harnesses: Control, visibility, and safe tool use
sessions.desc: As organizations build agentic systems that call tools, retrieve data, and take action, security must move beyond prompt-level controls. This session explores how to secure agentic harnesses with the visibility, policy, and access controls needed to make tool-using AI safe and governable in production. Learn to implement authentication, authorization, logging, and policy enforcement across model calls, tools, and retrieval flows — keeping agents useful without giving them unchecked reach. Also learn practical patterns for controlling agent behavior, reducing risk from unsafe tool use, and making agentic systems auditable and operationally defensible.

speakers.name: Gérard Zapf
speakers.title: Principal Specialist Solution Engineer - Cloudflare One

sessions.title: State under siege: How Estonia stopped Russia’s DDoS campaigns
sessions.desc: Estonia knows what nation-state DDoS looks like. As Russia’s aggression has intensified, Estonian government websites, media, and critical public services have faced sustained, politically timed volumetric attacks designed to paralyze Estonian society. In the first half of 2026, Cloudflare observed a surge in attacks exceeding 1 Tbps, with DNS floods emerging as the dominant vector and geopolitical flashpoints driving campaign timing. In this panel discussion, Estonia’s Information System Authority shares how it built a proactive national cyber defense posture with Cloudflare’s global network and threat intelligence and what defenders everywhere can learn from a country that has been on the front line a long time.

speakers.name: Brian Carter
speakers.title: Threat Research Director – Cybercrime, Cloudforce One – PREDICT

sessions.title: The integrated Cloudflare stack for trusted AI adoption
sessions.desc: AI adoption is moving fast, but trusted adoption requires a control plane that can keep pace. This session explores how the integrated Cloudflare stack connects visibility, policy enforcement, data protection, and operational control into a practical model for secure AI. See how to secure AI traffic, reduce data exposure, and apply consistent governance across users, applications, and AI services without adding friction. With a focus on real-world architecture and day-to-day operations, this session helps practitioners gain a clear, deployable approach to building an integrated control plane that balances security with adoption.

sessions.title: What security leaders really want from AI governance
sessions.desc: Security leaders want practical, visible, and enforceable AI governance — not business roadblocks. Join security leaders and Cloudflare experts to explore what it takes to govern enterprise AI: reducing data leakage, exposing shadow AI, enforcing realistic policies, and keeping pace with rapid adoption. Explore tradeoffs between innovation and control, how to operationalize governance without friction, and where current tooling falls short. Leave with a clear view of modern AI governance needs and a framework that balances protection with productivity.

sessions.title: Screaming in the Cloud: Live interview with Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht
sessions.desc: In this episode of Screaming in the Cloud, host Corey Quinn will be joined by Dane Knecht, CTO of Cloudflare. They will engage in a wide-ranging discussion on the evolution of cloud computing, tracing how infrastructure is shifting from traditional cloud workloads toward an agentic cloud designed for autonomous AI agents. Along the way, Dane pulls back the curtain on Cloudflare’s own internal AI deployment. It’ll be a conversation about scale, resilience, and what happens to infrastructure philosophy when the Internet stops being mostly human.

sessions.title: A test AI can’t pass
sessions.desc: Proof of humanity in the age of AI. Join Tiago Sada, Chief Product Officer at Tools for Humanity, building for World, to explore why the future of trust on the Internet needs to start in the physical world. This session is sponsored by Tools for Humanity.
